4 boneless, tied lamb sirloin rolls (about 2 pounds) or 8 double-thick lamb chops (about 6 pounds), trimmed of fat
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
1 tablespoon unsalted butter at room temperature (optional)
Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
m: Stir the garlic, mint, ground coffee, ¼ cup oil and ⅓ cup wine together in a non-reactive bowl.
Grind the peppercorns, cumin, mustard and coriander seeds, rosemary and salt in a mortar or spice grinder and whisk into the coffee mixture.
Rub the marinade all over the lamb in a glass dish, cover and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours; wipe off most, but not all, of it with paper towels.
Cook the mushrooms and shallots in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, add the 1½ cups wine, vanilla bean and mint, boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the stock, brewed coffee and honey and reduce by half again; remove the vanilla bean and thicken with the cornstarch slurry.
Off the heat swirl in the butter, season and keep warm.
Grill the lamb over a hot fire 7 to 8 minutes per side to medium-rare; plate with the sauce on top and mint sprigs.

i: 1 4- to 5-pound boned leg of veal, rolled and tied
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 red onion, peeled and thinly sliced
2 cups sliced portobello mushrooms, stems trimmed, inner gills removed
3 cups sliced shiitake mushrooms, stems trimmed
1 cup Pinot Noir or other red wine
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: chopped parsley, whole roasted shiitake mushrooms
m: Rub the veal with the paprika, salt and pepper; heat the oven to 325°F.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and herbs in the olive oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes until the onion is translucent, then spoon into a foil-lined roasting pan big enough for the veal.
Brown the roast lightly on all sides in the butter in the same pan and set it on the mushroom bed.
Pour over the wine and 1¼ cups stock and roast about 2 hours to an internal temperature of 170°F, basting occasionally.
Cut the string and tent the veal in foil; purée the mushroom mixture until smooth, thin with stock if you like, season and keep warm.
Slice the veal over a pool of mushroom sauce, scatter with walnuts, parsley and whole mushrooms; glazed dilled carrots and roasted potato quarters go well.

WLC|white bean soup with escargots and o.s: 6 to 8 as an appetizer or 4 as an entrée
i: 12 ounces white beans (such as Great Northern), rinsed and picked over
¾ cup cored, chopped fresh fennel
1 cup plum tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1 pound Yukon gold or new potatoes, diced
2 teaspoons chopped fresh rosemary (1 teaspoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
¾ teaspoon chopped fresh rosemary (⅓ teaspoon dried)
m: Soak the beans overnight in cold water, then drain and discard any discoloured ones.
Sauté the carrot, celery, onions, fennel and garlic in 1½ tablespoons oil over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes in a large pot.
Add the beans, stock, tomatoes, potatoes, rosemary, mustard seed and fennel seed, boil, then cover and simmer 45 to 55 minutes until the beans are al dente; season.
Stir the olive paste, shallots, balsamic and rosemary together for the relish.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil, cook the garlic and escargots 3 to 4 minutes until warmed through, add the Pernod and cook 1 minute until it evaporates.
Ladle the soup into hot bowls, dollop relish on top, arrange the escargots around it and add rosemary sprigs.

i: 1 cup warm tap water (110° to 115°F on an instant-read thermometer)
¼ cup plus ½ tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
2½ tablespoons chopped mixed herbs (parsley, basil, oregano)
2½ tablespoons chopped sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
1 cup fresh or frozen okra, sliced in half lengthwise
3 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1½ tablespoons dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
12 ounces hot Italian, andouille, or chorizo sausage, cut into ¼-inch slices
1 cup grated Asiago or Parmesan cheese
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Dissolve the sugar and yeast in the warm water and leave 8 to 10 minutes until foamy, then stir in ¼ cup oil for 15 to 20 seconds.
Pulse the flour, salt and pepper in a food processor, add the herbs and sun-dried tomatoes, then pour in the yeast mixture with the motor running until a ball forms, 30 to 45 seconds.
Knead on a floured surface 5 to 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, adjusting with warm water or flour as needed.
Turn the dough in a bowl coated with ½ tablespoon oil, cover with plastic and let rise in a warm spot about 1½ hours until doubled.
Sauté the okra, mushrooms, celery, carrots, onions, garlic, basil and oregano in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat 7 to 8 minutes.
Brown the sausage slices in a non-stick pan 5 to 6 minutes and blot dry.
Whisk the tomato sauce, paste, filé and cayenne, then fold in the sausage, prosciutto, cheese and vegetables; season.
Heat the oven to 450°F. Punch down the dough, divide in four and roll into 8- to 9-inch rounds; brush with oil.
Fill one half of each round, fold over, roll and crimp the edges, press with a fork, brush with oil and prick the tops.
Bake on a cornmeal-dusted sheet on the top rack 16 to 18 minutes until golden, shielding the edges with foil if they darken; serve with basil leaves.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh marjoram (½ tablespoon dried)
1 10-ounce package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 roasted yellow bell peppers (see page 116), peeled and seeded
¼ cup lightly toasted pine nuts
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil (½ tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Soften the onions and garlic in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, add the veal, oregano, marjoram, fennel seed and Worcestershire and cook 5 to 6 minutes until no longer pink; drain the fat.
Stir in the spinach and eggs for 2 to 3 minutes, then off the heat mix in the mozzarella, ricotta and bread crumbs; season with the salt, pepper, pepper flakes and cinnamon and cool.
Boil the manicotti 7 to 8 minutes (or per the package) until firm but cooked, hold in cold water, drain and pat dry.
Fill the tubes with the veal mixture, lay in an oiled baking dish and refrigerate.
Blend the roasted peppers, shallot, pine nuts and Worcestershire until smooth, stream in the oil, season and chill; bring to room temperature to serve.

For the sauce, cook the onions and garlic in ½ tablespoon oil 5 to 6 minutes, add the sherry, tomato sauce, tomatoes, paste, oregano, basil, sugar and pepper flakes and cook 7 to 8 minutes, stirring; season.
Pour the sauce over the manicotti, cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 30 minutes, then top with the grated mozzarella and bake uncovered 15 minutes more.
Serve two manicotti per plate with a dollop of pesto and a sprinkle of oregano.

i: ¾ tablespoon all-purpose flour plus more as needed
1 fennel bulb, cored and thinly sliced (about 2 cups)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
½ cup pitted, chopped Kalamata olives
m: Rinse and dry the chicken, season with salt and pepper flakes and dust lightly with flour.
Brown the chicken on all sides in the butter and oil in a large stockpot over medium heat; drain on paper towels.
In the same pot sauté the garlic, onions, mushrooms, fennel, carrots, sage and rosemary 7 to 8 minutes.
Return the chicken with the stock, wine, tomatoes, tomato paste and olives, cover and simmer 50 to 55 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, reduce the sauce 15 minutes uncovered, then put the chicken back to heat through; season.
Serve in bowls with parsley and wedges of baked polenta topped with Parmesan.

i: ⅔ cup blood orange (or regular orange) juice
½ teaspoon blood orange (or regular orange) zest
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
1 tablespoon unsalted butter at room temperature (optional)
GARNISH: thin slices of blood orange
m: Whisk the marinade ingredients in a non-reactive bowl and pour over the tenderloins in a glass dish; refrigerate covered 3 to 4 hours, turning once.
Pat the pork dry, keep the marinade, and spread the mustard over the meat.
Simmer the marinade with the stock and cherries in a large pan about 15 minutes until it coats a wooden spoon.
Thicken slightly with the cornstarch slurry, whisk in the butter if using and keep warm.
Grill over hot coals 6 to 7 minutes, turn and cook 4 to 5 minutes more to medium-rare and juicy.
Slice, spoon over the sauce and garnish with blood orange slices.

i: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 spicy sausages (spicy Italian, andouille, or chorizo), cut in ½-inch slices
8 ounces mussels, debearded and rinsed (see page 58)
1 large roasted red pepper, diced (see page 116)
¾ cup fresh or defrosted frozen peas
m: Rinse and dry the thighs, rub with ¼ teaspoon salt and the pepper and rest a few minutes.
Brown the chicken on both sides in ½ tablespoon oil in a non-stick pan; drain on paper towels.

In a paella pan fry the sausage and escargots in the remaining 2 tablespoons oil 3 to 4 minutes, add the garlic and onions for 3 minutes, then the rice, remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, saffron, paprika and turmeric and stir 5 minutes to coat.
Add the wine and let it evaporate, then the stock; bring to a boil and drop to a simmer.
Nestle the chicken and mussels over the rice, cover and cook 17 to 18 minutes until the chicken is done and the rice al dente.
Scatter the roasted pepper, parsley and peas on top, cover 2 to 3 minutes just to warm, keeping the peas bright; season.
Finish with more parsley and serve from the pan, one thigh each with the mussels and escargots shared out.

WLC|basil fettuccine with sun-dried toma.s: 5 to 6 as an appetizer or 2 to 4 as an entrée
i: 1¼ cups sliced crimini or shiitake mushrooms
¾ cup Zinfandel or other red wine
1 cup julienned sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
⅔ cup pitted, chopped Kalamata olives
3 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1½ tablespoons dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1¼ pounds fresh or dried basil fettuccine noodles
½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
m: Cook the garlic, onions and mushrooms in the oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until the onions are translucent.
Add the wine, sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste, tomato sauce, olives, basil, fennel seed and balsamic and simmer, stirring, about 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Keep warm over low heat, loosening with more wine if it gets too thick; season lightly, remembering the prosciutto is salty.
Cook the fettuccine in salted boiling water 3 to 5 minutes until al dente, drain and return to the pot over medium heat.
Divide the noodles between plates, spoon over the sauce and top with Parmesan, prosciutto and walnuts; scatter with basil and serve at once.

i: 1 teaspoon fines herbes (see page 36) or dried oregano
m: Slice the eggplants lengthwise ¼ inch thick, salt with 1 teaspoon and leave on paper towels 30 minutes; rinse, dry and roast on an oiled sheet at 375°F for 30 minutes.
Brown the lamb with the onions and garlic over medium-high heat, crumbling it; drain in a strainer and blot on paper towels.
Return the meat to the cleaned pan with the remaining salt, pepper, nutmeg, cinnamon, fines herbes, parsley and tomato paste; add the wine and simmer 10 minutes.
Grease a 9-by-13-inch dish and dust with the bread crumbs, holding back 3 tablespoons.
For the sauce, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then stir in the milk, nutmeg and salt until thick.
Temper the egg yolk with a little hot sauce, add the reserved crumbs, and blend back into the sauce.
Layer eggplant, meat and plenty of feta; repeat, then top with the sauce.
Sprinkle with Parmesan and bake at 350°F for 50 to 60 minutes until golden. Cut in squares and garnish with parsley.

i: 4½ pounds chicken breasts, thighs, and legs
⅓ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ cup pitted, sliced Spanish green olives
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon cold water
m: Rinse and dry the chicken and dust all over with the salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons of the flour.
Cook the pancetta in the butter in a large pot over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes, then brown the chicken in batches about 5 minutes a side; set on paper towels.
Brown the remaining tablespoon of flour in the pot 1 to 2 minutes, then cook the onions, mushrooms, garlic and herbs 5 minutes.
Add the wine, tomatoes, tomato paste, stock and chicken; boil, then cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Add the pearl onions and olives and cook 10 minutes more. Lift out the chicken and keep warm under foil.
Stir the cornstarch slurry and mustard into the liquid and boil hard 6 to 7 minutes to thicken; season.
Serve the chicken in bowls with plenty of sauce and parsley, with rice or pasta and garlic bread.

i: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 pounds cubed pork stew meat (from the shoulder or roast)
2 stalks celery, ends trimmed and diced
1 large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped
2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (1 tablespoon dried)
12 ounces tomatillos, husked, rinsed, and cut into quarters
1 roasted red pepper, seeded and chopped (see page 116)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Soak the beans 8 hours or overnight (or boil and stand 1 hour in the hot water); drain, rinse and pick over.
Toss the pork in the chili powder, cumin, cayenne, achiote, basil, pepper and salt.
Cook the pancetta in a heavy pot until barely browned; remove it and pour off the fat.
Heat the oil and sauté the pork, garlic, onion, celery, red pepper, jalapeños and oregano 7 to 8 minutes until the pork colours.
Return the pancetta and add the wine, stock, beans, cilantro, bay leaf and cloves; boil, then cover and simmer 1 hour.
For the salsa, sauté the tomatillos, onion, shallot, garlic, jalapeño, roasted pepper and cumin in the oil 10 to 12 minutes until softening; cool, then stir in the cilantro and season.
Ladle the stew into bowls, top with salsa and a dollop of sour cream, and add cilantro sprigs; serve with garlic bread or corn tortillas.

i: 1½ tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (¾ tablespoon dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ leg of lamb, boned, butterflied, and trimmed of most fat (about 2 pounds meat)
1 large whole head of garlic, unpeeled
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Mix the marinade, seal it with the lamb in a plastic bag and refrigerate at least 2 to 3 hours, turning now and then. Pat the lamb dry.
Trim the tip off the garlic head, drizzle with the oil, season, wrap loosely in foil and roast at 350°F for 45 to 50 minutes; squeeze out the cloves.
For the sauce, soften the shallots in the oil 2 to 3 minutes, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the stock, mint, roasted garlic and mustard and reduce by half again; season.
Grill the lamb over a hot fire 8 to 9 minutes a side for medium-rare, taking the thin end pieces off first.
Slice, spoon over the sauce and scatter with mint.

i: ⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 rehydrated dried chipotle pepper, stemmed and minced, or ¼ teaspoon chipotle chiles in adobo (see page 175)
4 ears fresh (or frozen) corn, husks removed
½ cup chopped roasted red bell pepper (see page 116)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade, bag it with the steak and refrigerate 4 to 5 hours, turning occasionally; drain, keeping the marinade for basting.
Rub the corn with olive oil and roast at 350°F for 45 minutes, then cut off the kernels (about 2 cups).
Cook the pancetta over low-medium heat 8 to 10 minutes until lightly browned; drain and blot.
Mix the corn with the pancetta, bell pepper, garlic, Worcestershire, jalapeños, vinegar and basil; season and chill, then bring to room temperature.
Grill the steak over a hot fire 5 minutes a side for rare, rest 5 minutes under foil and slice thinly against the grain on an angle.
Spoon salsa onto each plate and top with slices of steak.

i: 12 ounces Italian sausage, cut into ½-inch slices
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper or red pepper flakes
1 pound dried penne or other small dried pasta
GARNISH: shredded Asiago cheese, chopped parsley
m: Soak the porcini in hot water 2 to 3 hours and drain.
Brown the sausage slices in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat 6 to 7 minutes; blot on paper towels.
In a large pan cook the onions and garlic 4 to 5 minutes until translucent, then add both mushrooms, the herbs, salt and pepper for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour in the Syrah, boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Add the tomatoes and tomato paste and simmer 8 to 10 minutes; return the sausage to heat through and season.
Boil the penne in salted water until al dente, drain, and toss with the sauce in the pot, reheating if needed.
Serve in four bowls topped with Asiago and parsley.

i: ¼ teaspoon fresh ground black pepper
1 6- to 7-pound whole leg of lamb, boned, butterflied, and trimmed of excess fat (about 4½ pounds meat)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
¼ cup pitted, sliced green olives
¼ cup pitted and sliced Kalamata olives
m: Whisk the marinade ingredients in a non-reactive bowl, pour into a large sealable bag with the lamb and marinate 4 to 6 hours, turning occasionally.
Sauté the shallots and mushrooms in the olive oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes, add the wine and boil down by half.
Add the stock and rosemary and reduce by half again.
Stir in the mustard and olives and simmer gently until the sauce coats a wooden spoon; keep warm.
Pat the lamb dry, keeping the marinade for basting, and grill over very hot coals 7 to 8 minutes a side to medium-rare, basting now and then; take the thin ends off early.
Rest under foil a few minutes, slice thinly and serve on warm plates with the sauce and rosemary sprigs; roasted potato quarters and tomatoes gratinée go well.

i: ¾ tablespoon whole mixed peppercorns, lightly crushed
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Oil the filets, press the crushed peppercorns and salt onto the tops and sides, and spread the tops with mustard.
Soften the garlic in the butter over low-medium heat 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the wine, vinegar, mustard, Worcestershire, stock, Cognac and tomato paste; boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Add the cream and reduce a little more to thicken; season and adjust the consistency.
Grill the filets over very hot coals 8 to 10 minutes, turn and give them 5 to 6 minutes more for rare, or longer to taste.
Pool the sauce on the plates and set the filets on top; asparagus and sweet potato purée suit it.

i: ½ teaspoon coriander seed, toasted and crushed
1½ tablespoons chopped, seeded pasilla chiles (see NOTE)
1 tablespoon chopped chipotle chiles in adobo (see NOTE)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
8 ounces feta cheese (tomato-basil, if available), cut into ¼-inch cubes
1 cup chopped, roasted, peeled, and seeded peppers (yellow and red bell peppers, Anaheim chiles)
m: Rub the pork all over with the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cumin, oregano and sage.
Brown it on all sides and both ends in the olive oil over medium heat; move to a baking dish and keep the oil in the pan.
Roast at 350°F about 1½ hours to an internal temperature of 165°F (indirect medium heat on a gas grill also works).
For the mole, cook the onions and garlic in the reserved pan 5 to 6 minutes, add the sesame seeds, spices, chiles and cilantro for 3 to 4 minutes, then add the stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend the mixture with the peanut butter, tomato paste, raisins, chocolate and lime juice until smooth; return to the pan and simmer covered 35 to 40 minutes, thinning with stock if needed. Season.
For the rice, sweat the shallots and onions in the butter and oil 4 to 5 minutes, then toast the rice, cumin, oregano and fennel seed 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the stock and tomatoes, boil, then simmer covered 10 to 12 minutes until nearly dry; stir in the feta and peppers, cover 5 to 7 minutes more, rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Slice the pork, spoon over the mole, serve the rice alongside and garnish with cilantro and lime.

i: 3 red bell peppers, halved and seeded
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon chopped fresh basil (½ teaspoon dried)
1 teaspoon chopped fresh oregano (½ teaspoon dried)
GARNISH: basil leaves, grated Parmesan cheese
m: Smoke the tomatoes, onions, peppers and shallots on foil-lined racks over wet fruitwood, oak or hickory chips for 2 to 3 hours, topping up the chips as needed.
Peel, seed, drain and chop the tomatoes; peel and chop the onions and shallots; seed and chop the peppers.

Sweat the onions, peppers, shallots and herbs in the oil 8 to 10 minutes, add the tomatoes, sherry, vinegar, tomato paste and roasted garlic and simmer uncovered 15 minutes; add the salt, pepper and pepper flakes.
Purée in batches about 45 seconds until smooth; keep 2 cups for the dish and freeze the rest.
Trim the duck breasts, cut small X slashes in the fat, and marinate skin side down with the oil, Worcestershire, hot sauce, salt, pepper, basil and oregano for 3 to 4 hours in the fridge.
Sear skin side down over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes, turn and cook 3 to 4 minutes to medium-rare.
Rest briefly, slice at an angle, top with the sauce and finish with basil leaves and Parmesan; garlicky sautéed spinach alongside.

i: ½ teaspoon toasted mustard seed, crushed
1 teaspoon chopped fresh thyme (½ teaspoon dried)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade, seal with the tenderloins in a plastic bag and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours; pat the pork dry and keep the marinade.
Oil the washed beets and roast at 350°F for 55 to 60 minutes until the skins shrivel; cool, peel and cut into ¼-inch dice.
Boil the marinade (minus the bay leaf) and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the cranberry juice, stock, vinegar and beets and reduce by half again, then add the cornstarch slurry and cook until thickened.
Off the heat swirl in the butter if using, season and keep warm.
Grill the pork over a hot fire 8 to 9 minutes, turn and cook 5 to 6 minutes more until medium-rare; rest in foil.
Spoon the sauce onto plates and set sliced pork on top with parsley; horseradish mashed potatoes alongside.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh tarragon leaves (½ tablespoon dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
4 green onions, ends trimmed and minced
1 tablespoon chopped fresh tarragon (1½ teaspoons dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 cup pitted and halved fresh cherries
m: Whisk the marinade in a non-reactive bowl, pour into a sealable bag with the venison and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours.
Boil the chow mein noodles in salted water 1½ minutes, stirring to separate; drain, cool in cold water and drain again.
Toss the noodles with the green onions, corn, tarragon, zest, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Press the mixture into a 12-inch non-stick pan of hot vegetable oil over medium heat and cook 6 to 7 minutes, flip, and cook 5 to 6 minutes more until golden and crisp; drain, quarter and keep warm.
Pat the venison dry and put the marinade in a pan with the stock and cherries; boil, then simmer until halved and coating a spoon.
Stir in the port and mustard and simmer 5 minutes more to thicken; season and swirl in the butter off the heat.
Grill the venison over red-hot coals 3 to 4 minutes a side, no more than medium-rare, slice thinly and serve with the sauce and noodle cake.

i: ⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 cups peeled and diced celery root
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ cup shredded smoked mozzarella cheese
m: Cut the veal into 1-inch cubes and dust with the flour, salt and pepper.
Brown the veal with the pancetta in the butter over medium heat 6 to 7 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, celery root, onions, garlic, paprika, caraway and fines herbes and cook 8 minutes more.
Pour in the stock and wine, boil, then cover and simmer 1¼ hours; season.
Serve piping hot, topped with the pecans and smoked mozzarella, with wild rice and sautéed spinach.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
8 ounces Gorgonzola cheese, cut into small chunks
¼ cup lightly toasted walnut halves
¾ tablespoon chopped roasted garlic (see page 164)
2 tablespoons herb-flavored (basil or oregano) or extra-virgin olive oil
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the oil, garlic, vinegar, rosemary, salt and pepper over the steaks in a glass dish and refrigerate covered 2 to 3 hours.
Process all the “butter” ingredients about a minute until well mixed; serve at room temperature.
Pour boiling stock over the bulgur, cover with foil and stand about 30 minutes until absorbed.
Stir the tomatoes, mint, chives, roasted garlic, green onions, paprika and oil into the bulgur and season.
Grill the steaks over a hot fire 5 to 6 minutes a side or to taste; soon after turning, mound some Gorgonzola butter on each to half-melt.
Serve with the tabbouleh and a dish of extra butter at the table.

i: 2 medium globe eggplants, cut horizontally in ½-inch slices
2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (1 tablespoon dried)
½ teaspoon fennel seed, toasted and crushed
m: Whisk the marinade, spoon it over the filets and refrigerate covered 2 to 3 hours.
Rub the eggplant slices with 1 tablespoon of the oil, salt them and roast at 350°F for 40 minutes; chop into ½-inch cubes.
Cook the onions in the remaining 1½ tablespoons oil over medium-high heat 3 to 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes, roasted garlic, herbs, fennel seed and eggplant and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring; season and keep warm.
Grill the filets over very hot coals 5 to 7 minutes a side for medium-rare or to taste.
Spoon the ragout onto plates with the filets beside it.

i: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1½ cups sliced crimini or shiitake mushrooms
½ cup red wine (preferably Cabernet Sauvignon)
¼ ounce dried morel or porcini mushrooms (rehydrated in cold water, drained, and halved)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
½ teaspoon cornstarch mixed with ½ teaspoon cold water
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade in a non-reactive bowl, pour over the chops in a glass dish and refrigerate covered 3 to 4 hours; pat dry.
Cook the shallots and crimini in the oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until the shallots turn golden.
Add the green peppercorns, vinegar and wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the stock and morels and reduce by half again.
Stir in the basil, mustard and cornstarch slurry to thicken until the sauce coats a spoon; season.
Grill the chops over hot coals 8 to 10 minutes, turn and cook 7 to 8 minutes more for medium-rare or to taste.
Top the chops with the sauce and chopped basil; sautéed fresh peas go alongside.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried, crushed)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ leg of lamb, butterflied and trimmed of excess fat (about 2 pounds net)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
1 cup seeded, chopped fresh plum tomatoes
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade, pour into a sealable bag with the lamb and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours; pat the lamb dry.
Soak the porcini in very hot water 45 minutes until soft, squeeze out the water and cut each into thirds.
Fry the pancetta in the oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, then add the onions, roasted garlic and basil and cook 6 to 7 minutes until translucent.
Add the wine and porcini and simmer 10 minutes to reduce by half.
Add the stock, mustard and tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon; season.
Grill the lamb over hot coals 8 to 9 minutes, turn and grill 7 to 8 minutes more until medium-rare; slice thinly.
Pool the sauce on plates, lay the lamb on top and sprinkle with parsley; serve with polenta cakes and winter squash.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (½ tablespoon dried)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (½ tablespoon dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon port or crème de cassis
2 tablespoons unsalted butter at room temperature
m: Combine the marinade in a sealable bag with the venison and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours or overnight; pat dry and keep the marinade.
Whiz the bread in a food processor about 1 minute, then add the shallots, sage, salt, pepper, mustard and oil for 20 to 30 seconds more.
Press the coating onto the top and sides of the venison and set it on a broiler pan.
Reduce the reserved marinade and wine by half in a large pan.

Add the stock, currants, port and mustard and reduce by half again until the sauce coats a spoon; strain, whisk in the butter and keep warm, adding a dash of balsamic if it tastes too sweet against the wine.
Broil the venison 7 to 8 minutes until rare; do not overcook.
Slice and serve with the currant sauce; corn fritters and sugar snap peas suit it.

i: 1 4½-pound prime rib roast of beef (2 ribs), trimmed and tied
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 teaspoons minced fresh rosemary (1 teaspoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ teaspoon cornstarch mixed with ½ teaspoon cold water
m: Set the roast fat side up on a rack in a flameproof roasting pan and coat it with ½ tablespoon mustard, ½ teaspoon horseradish, ¾ tablespoon rosemary, the salt and pepper; roast at 450°F for 20 minutes.
Toss the onion, shallot, carrots, celery and mushrooms with a little olive oil, salt and pepper in a baking dish; lower the oven to 350°F and roast the vegetables on a rack below the beef for 1 hour.
Blend the flour, eggs, milk, chives, rosemary and salt until smooth and chill covered at least 45 minutes.
Take out the vegetables and chop roughly; give the roast 10 minutes more to rare or medium-rare, then rest it under foil 20 to 30 minutes. Keep the pan unwashed.
Heat the oven to 425°F, melt the butter and oil in a shallow dish 3 to 4 minutes, pour in the chilled batter and bake 18 to 20 minutes until risen and golden; cut in four.
Deglaze the roasting pan with the Cabernet over medium heat, scraping, 6 to 7 minutes until halved.
Add the stock, the remaining ½ tablespoon mustard, ½ teaspoon horseradish and 1 tablespoon rosemary, and the vegetables; reduce by half, thicken with the cornstarch slurry and season.
Carve into four portions, spoon over the jus, sprinkle with chives and serve the pudding alongside.

i: ¼ pound (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup cold water plus more as needed for filling
GARNISH: crème fraîche or whipped cream, mint sprigs
m: Pulse the flour, sugar and cinnamon with the butter to coarse pea-sized meal, add the salt dissolved in the water and blend just until the dough comes together.
Roll to an 11-inch circle ⅛ inch thick, fit into a 10-inch removable-bottom tart pan and chill 15 minutes.
Prick the shell, line with foil, fill with weights and bake at 400°F on a sheet 15 to 20 minutes until light golden; remove the foil and weights and cool fully.
Simmer the apricots, peaches, port and 1 cup water 8 to 10 minutes until soft; strain, keeping the fruit, and top the liquid up with cold water to 1 cup.
Whisk ¼ cup of the liquid with the brown sugar and cornstarch; return the rest to the pot with the slurry and orange juice.
Boil, stirring, then simmer until thickened; stir in the fruit and pecans, cool completely and pour into the shell.
Unmould onto a plate and serve chilled or at room temperature with crème fraîche and mint.

i: ¼ pound (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces
6 cups peeled, sliced green apples (about 4 to 5 medium apples)
2 tablespoons all-purpose flour, tapioca flour, or instant tapioca
GARNISH: small wedges of Stilton cheese
m: Pulse the flour, sugar and cinnamon with the butter to coarse pea-sized meal, add the salt dissolved in the water and blend just until the dough gathers.
Roll to an 11-inch circle ⅛ inch thick, fit into a 9-inch pie pan, trim the overhang and chill 15 minutes.
Gently toss all the filling ingredients together in a large bowl.
Fork together the flour, brown sugar and crystallized ginger, then rub in the butter until no lumps show.
Fill the shell, scatter over the streusel and crimp the edge.
Bake on a sheet in the middle of a 375°F oven about 1 hour until golden and bubbling, shielding the rim with foil from 35 to 40 minutes in until 55 minutes.
Cool and serve each slice with a small wedge of Stilton.

i: ½ pound (2 sticks) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tablespoon fresh lemon or lime juice
m: Pulse the flour, sugar and cinnamon with the butter to coarse pea-sized meal, add the salt dissolved in the water and blend just until it comes together; divide into two balls.
Wrap one round and chill it for the lattice; roll the other to an 11-inch circle ⅛ inch thick, line a 9-inch pie pan and refrigerate.
Mix the apricots and berries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, cinnamon and cardamom and stand at least 15 minutes.
Pour the filling into the shell.
Roll the second round to 11 inches, cut 8 to 10 strips ½ inch wide, weave them crisscross on top, pinch the ends into the base and flute or fork the edge.
Wrap the rim in a 2- to 3-inch band of foil and bake in the middle of a 425°F oven 55 to 60 minutes until golden and bubbling, removing the foil 15 to 20 minutes before the end.

i: 2 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into bits
m: Heat the oven to 400°F and lay the figs cut side up in a buttered 8-by-8-by-2-inch dish with the raspberries scattered over.
Grind the almonds finely with the flour in a blender or processor.
Add ⅓ cup sugar, the eggs, milk and port and blend smooth, scraping down the sides.
Pour the batter over the fruit, dot with the butter and sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons sugar.
Bake in the middle of the oven 30 to 40 minutes until golden and set; cool 20 minutes and dust with powdered sugar.

i: ¼ cup quick-cooking tapioca or tapioca flour
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter or margarine
m: Mix the sugar, tapioca, cinnamon and orange peel in a shallow 2-quart baking dish.
Add the rhubarb, berries and lime juice, toss well and stand at least 30 minutes, stirring a few times to soften the tapioca.
Blend the flour, butter, brown sugar and nutmeg until lumpy and crumble evenly over the fruit.
Bake in the middle of a 375°F oven about 35 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Cool on a rack 15 to 20 minutes and serve, with lemon sorbet if you like.

i: 5 ounces (10 tablespoons) unsalted butter at room temperature
1 pound brioche, challah, or egg bread, cut into ½-inch-thick slices
2 pounds fresh peaches, poached, skinned, pitted, and sliced or one 29-ounce can, drained
m: Heat the oven to 275°F; butter the bread lightly on both sides and toast it in the oven.
Purée half the peaches, keep half the purée for garnish, and mix the rest with the sliced peaches and bananas.
Whisk the eggs, then ¾ cup of the sugar and the milk, hard for 2 minutes; stir in the fruit.
Butter a 3-inch-deep loaf pan generously and dust with 2 tablespoons of the remaining sugar.
Layer bread and fruit custard alternately until ½ inch from the top; stand 1 hour.
Mix the cinnamon into the last of the sugar, sprinkle over, cover with foil and bake 1 hour 15 minutes.
Rest 2 hours at room temperature and serve with mint sprigs and the reserved purée.

i: ½ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
Eighteen ½-inch-thick baguette slices, cut on a wide diagonal
Crème fraîche and trout roe, for serving
m: Heat a grill. Swish the escarole heads, root end up, in a bowl of cold water to rinse out grit, then shake dry.
Whisk the ½ cup olive oil with thyme and garlic. Brush it over the escarole and season with salt and pepper.
Grill the escarole over moderate heat about 20 minutes, basting with the garlic oil now and then, until charred and tender.
Cool the escarole, chop it roughly and toss with any leftover garlic oil, salt and pepper.
Oil and season the bread slices and grill about 2 minutes, until marked on both sides.
Pile escarole on each toast, add a spoonful of crème fraîche and some trout roe.

i: Two 7-oz. cans tuna packed in water, drained well and flaked
m: Gently mix the tuna, scallions, capers, parsley, olive oil and harissa; season with salt and pepper.
Make two stacks of three phyllo sheets and cut each stack across into four 4-by-12-inch strips; keep them under a damp towel.
Put a generous ¼ cup of filling at the near end of a strip and brush the far end with egg.
Fold the phyllo over the filling into a triangle and keep folding flag-style to the end; press to seal. Repeat.
Heat ¼ inch of canola oil in a cast-iron skillet until shimmering.
Fry four triangles at a time over moderately low heat, turning, 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

i: One 14-oz. package all-butter puff pastry, thawed if frozen but still cold
m: Combine the three kinds of seeds with the dried onion, salt and garlic powder.
Line three baking sheets with parchment.
On a floured counter roll the pastry to 11 by 14 inches and halve it lengthwise.
Brush with egg wash, scatter the seed mix over, then slice crosswise into ¾-inch strips.
Twist each strip and set on the sheets 2 inches apart; freeze 30 minutes until firm.
Bake at 375° about 22 minutes until golden, rotating the sheets halfway. Cool about 10 minutes before serving.

i: ½ cup white cheese powder, such as King Arthur Vermont Cheese Powder
½ tsp. ground dried lime zest or 1 tsp. finely grated lime zest
m: Stir together the cheese powder, salt, chipotle powder, cilantro, lime zest and cayenne.
Put the oil and popcorn kernels in a large covered saucepan over moderately high heat.
Once popping starts, shake the pan regularly until it stops, 3 to 5 minutes.
Tip into a big bowl, toss with the melted butter, then toss with the cheese seasoning and serve.

i: 2 baking potatoes, peeled and grated on the large holes of a box grater
1 Granny Smith apple, peeled and grated on the large holes of a box grater
m: Wring out as much liquid as possible from the grated potato and apple.
Toss them in a bowl with the dill, flour, salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large nonstick skillet and add four ¼-cup mounds, pressing them flat.
Fry over moderately high heat about 2 minutes a side, adding another tablespoon of oil when you flip, until crisp and golden.
Drain briefly on paper towels and repeat with the rest. Serve with sour cream.

i: 10 fingerling potatoes, scrubbed and halved lengthwise
Chives cut into twenty 1-inch lengths, for garnish
m: Heat the oven to 400°. Toss the potato halves with oil, salt and pepper on a rimmed sheet.
Roast cut side down about 25 minutes until tender and browned underneath; let cool to warm.
Roll the pressed caviar between plastic wrap into a 5-by-6-inch sheet about ⅛ inch thick and cut into 20 diamonds.
Turn the potatoes cut side up, add a dab of sour cream, a caviar diamond and a piece of chive. Serve at once.

i: 1 lb. shelled and deveined shrimp, chopped
m: Stir the mayonnaise with the hot sauce for a dipping sauce.
Combine shrimp, panko, eggs, scallions, lemon zest, smoked paprika, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper.
Shape into eight cakes about ¾ inch thick.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and fry the cakes in batches over moderately high heat, about 4 minutes total, flipping once, until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the spicy mayo and lemon wedges.

i: 1 tsp. pimentón de la Vera (smoked Spanish paprika)
1 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
3 large, very firm baking potatoes (about 2 lbs.), peeled and cut into ½-inch-thick sticks
m: Blend the mayo, garlic, smoked paprika and lemon juice in a food processor; stir in 2 tsp parsley, season and chill.
Rinse the potato sticks and dry them very well.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 250° and fry the potatoes in batches about 6 minutes, until nearly tender but pale. Drain.
Raise the oil to 350° and fry again in batches about 3 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain, salt right away, sprinkle with the remaining parsley and serve with the aioli.

i: One 1-inch-thick slice of provolone cheese (½ lb.)
m: Heat the oven to 450° and get a cast-iron skillet very hot on the stove.
Put in the provolone and sprinkle with half the oregano and half the pepper flakes.
Cook over moderate heat about 2 minutes until the underside browns, then flip and brown the other side about 2 minutes.
Scatter on the rest of the oregano and pepper flakes and the tomatoes.
Bake about 4 minutes until molten and the tomatoes are warm. Salt, add basil and serve with bread.

i: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ lb. brussels sprouts, thinly sliced (about 3 cups)
m: Boil the spaghetti in salted water until al dente.
Meanwhile heat ¼ cup oil in a large nonstick skillet and cook the sprouts and sausage over moderately high heat about 5 minutes, until the meat is browned and cooked.
Add the panko and stir about 3 minutes until crunchy; add chives, salt and pepper.
Drain the pasta, spoon the sausage mixture over, drizzle with oil and serve with lemon.

i: 1 large leek, white and light green parts only, thinly sliced
2½ lbs. celery root, peeled and cut into 1-inch dice (8 cups)
One 2-inch chunk of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (1 oz.), plus ¼ cup freshly grated cheese
2 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Melt the butter in a large saucepan and soften the leek and garlic over moderate heat, about 5 minutes.
Add the celery root, the Parmesan chunk, the stock and 5 cups water; bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over moderately low heat about 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the celery root is soft.
While it cooks, toast the walnuts at 375° for 5 to 7 minutes, cool and chop finely.
Mix the walnuts with the olive oil, parsley and grated cheese for the gremolata.
Blend the soup in two batches until very smooth, return to a clean pot, add the cream, season and reheat.
Ladle into bowls and spoon gremolata on top.

i: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
2 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
One 8-oz. baking potato, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
2 lbs. broccoli, stems peeled and sliced, florets cut into ½-inch pieces
4 oz. sourdough or ciabatta bread, cut into ½-inch dice
m: Heat the oven to 400°. In a big pot warm ¼ cup oil and cook the onion and garlic with salt and pepper 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and lightly browned.
Add 2 cups water, the stock, potato, broccoli stems and two-thirds of the florets; boil, then simmer about 30 minutes until everything is very soft.
Stir in the spinach just until it wilts.
Toss the leftover florets with 1 Tbsp oil and the bread cubes with the last 1 Tbsp oil; season both.
Roast the florets on half a sheet pan 10 minutes, then add the bread to the other half and roast about 10 minutes more until both are crisp.
Blend the soup in batches until silky, add the vinegar and season.
Serve topped with the crispy florets, croutons and chives.

i: 1 tsp. finely grated peeled fresh ginger
1 small head of bok choy (about ¾ lb.), cut into 1-inch pieces
¾ lb. asparagus, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
m: Heat the oven to 325°. Warm the vegetable oil in an ovenproof skillet and sizzle the scallions, ginger and garlic about 30 seconds.
Add the bok choy and cook about 2 minutes until wilted.
Add the asparagus and ½ tsp salt and cook about 3 minutes until nearly tender.
Spread the vegetables evenly, pour in the eggs with the pepper and remaining salt, and cook untouched about 2 minutes until the edge sets.
Bake about 25 minutes until firm, then drizzle with sesame oil and serve.

i: ½ lb. cauliflower florets, cut into 1-inch pieces
6 oz. Gruyère cheese, shredded (2 lightly packed cups)
m: Boil the cauliflower in salted water about 7 minutes until very soft; drain, pat dry, mash and let it drain in a colander until cool.
Heat the oven to 350°. Butter a 6-cup soufflé dish with 1 Tbsp butter and set it on a rimmed sheet.
Melt the remaining butter, whisk in the flour and cook about 3 minutes until bubbling.
Slowly whisk in the milk, bring to a boil and simmer about 7 minutes, whisking, until thick. Season and let cool in a large bowl.
Stir in the cauliflower, then fold in the Gruyère and chives.
Whisk the eggs until foamy and fold them gently into the base.
Pour into the dish and bake about 1 hour 10 minutes until risen and browned. Serve immediately.

i: ¼ cup finely diced peeled Asian pear
¼ cup peeled, seeded and finely diced cucumber
12 freshly shucked oysters on the half shell, such as Rappahannocks
m: Toast the coriander seeds in a dry pan over moderate heat about 2 minutes, cool, then crack them in a mortar.
Stir the coriander together with the pear, cucumber, chile, cilantro, lime juice, ginger, fish sauce, oil, salt and pepper.
Set the oysters on a bed of crushed ice.
Spoon a little relish onto each and serve straight away with the extra relish alongside.

i: ½ lb. prosciutto, sliced ½ inch thick
1 stick plus 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into thin slices
4 oz. curly spinach, coarsely chopped (4 cups)
2 tsp. fennel pollen or ½ tsp. ground fennel
½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
m: Dice the prosciutto and freeze about 30 minutes until very firm, then pulse in a food processor until finely chopped.
Blanch the 1 lb spinach about 1 minute, cool, squeeze completely dry and chop (about ½ cup).
Beat the ricotta smooth, then mix in the prosciutto, spinach, mascarpone, yolks and Parmesan; salt it and chill about 30 minutes.
For the dough, whisk the 00 flour and salt, add the 12 yolks and 1 Tbsp water to a well, and work into a shaggy dough with a fork.
Knead on a semolina-dusted surface about 5 minutes until smooth, wrap and rest 45 minutes.
Roll a quarter of the dough at a time through a pasta machine, twice on each of the first five settings, once on the sixth; halve and roll each half once on the thinnest.
Dot one sheet with two rows of eight teaspoon-size filling balls 1 inch apart, brush around them with water and cover with a second sheet.
Press out the air around each mound and cut with a 2-inch fluted cutter; keep on a semolina-dusted tray under a towel. You should get 64.
Boil the ravioli in two batches about 2 minutes until the edges are tender; save 1 cup cooking water.
In two skillets melt 4 Tbsp butter each with ¼ cup pasta water and half the chopped spinach; cook about 1 minute until wilted, then add half the ravioli to each and coat.
Move ravioli to a bowl; combine the pan juices in one skillet with the last 2 Tbsp butter, 1 tsp fennel pollen and ¼ cup cheese and swirl about 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Pour over the ravioli and finish with the remaining fennel pollen and cheese.

FW|extra-crispy fried chicken.t: 1 hr 15 min active; 4 hr 30 min total
i: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. kosher salt
1½ Tbsp. minced rosemary, plus 4 medium sprigs
5 minced bay leaves, preferably fresh, plus 5 whole leaves
3 garlic cloves, minced, plus 1 head broken into cloves
1 Tbsp. hot sauce, such as Tabasco
Grapeseed or vegetable oil, for frying
m: Heat the oven to 200°. Mix 3 Tbsp kosher salt, 2 Tbsp pepper, the olive oil and the minced herbs, bay and garlic; rub over both chickens.
Roast about 2½ hours, until the inner thigh reads 150°. Cool and cut each bird into 10 pieces.
Whisk the buttermilk, hot sauce and sugar, add the chicken, and refrigerate 1 hour.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 375° with the herb sprigs, whole bay leaves and garlic cloves; lift them out once crisp and golden.
Whisk both flours with the garlic and onion powders and the remaining 3 Tbsp salt and 2 Tbsp pepper.
Lift half the chicken from the buttermilk, dredge in the flour and fry over high heat until golden and 160° inside, about 6 minutes for breasts, 8 for other pieces.
Drain, bring the oil back to 375° and fry the rest.
Pile on a platter with the fried herbs and garlic, sprinkle with flaky salt and serve with lemon.

i: ¼ tsp. chipotle or other smoked chile powder
½ lb. mustard greens, thick stems discarded and leaves chopped
⅓ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Heat 2 Tbsp oil and cook the onion over moderately high heat about 5 minutes until soft and starting to color.
Add the garlic and all the spices and stir about 2 minutes until aromatic; let cool.
Combine the onion mixture with the veal, breadcrumbs, cream, egg and salt; roll into 1½-inch balls.
Brown the meatballs in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil in a large skillet over moderately high heat, about 5 minutes.
Push them aside, pour off all but 2 Tbsp fat, add the greens and stock, cover and cook about 4 minutes until wilted.
Serve the meatballs and greens in bowls.

i: 3 heads of radicchio (2 lbs.)—halved, cored and chopped into 1-inch pieces
m: Soak the chopped onion in the two vinegars at room temperature for 1 hour.
Meanwhile soak the radicchio in ice water for 15 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Lift out and discard the onion; whisk the honey and olive oil into the flavored vinegar.
Toss the radicchio with the dressing and 1 cup of the Manchego; season with salt and pepper.
Heap on a platter and scatter the remaining ½ cup cheese over the top.

i: 12 oz. skinless, boneless chicken breast cutlets, pounded ⅛ inch thick and very thinly sliced crosswise
1 Tbsp. finely chopped peeled fresh ginger
12 dried red chiles, such as chiles de árbol—10 left whole, 2 stemmed and crumbled
1 lb. seedless cucumbers, preferably Persian, cut into 1½-inch pieces
Lemon wedges and steamed rice, for serving
m: Toss the chicken with half the garlic and ginger plus the baking soda, salt and pepper.
Stir the vinegar, sugar and ¼ cup water together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a large skillet until shimmering and stir-fry the chicken over moderately high heat about 2 minutes, until nearly done; set aside.
Add the last 1 Tbsp oil, all the dried chiles, the cucumbers, the vinegar mixture and the rest of the garlic and ginger; season.
Stir-fry over moderate heat about 3 minutes until the cucumbers soften and the liquid mostly cooks off.
Return the chicken with the serrano and cook about 1 minute more until done; stir in cilantro and season.
Serve with lemon wedges and rice.

i: 1 Tbsp. crème fraîche or sour cream
2 bunches of arugula (¼ lb. each), tough stems discarded
m: Cut away all the peel and white pith from the oranges, tangerines and clementines.
Slice the clementines into ½-inch rounds, removing seeds, and put them in a bowl.
Over the same bowl, cut the orange and tangerine segments free of their membranes. Add the shallot and mint.
Whisk the lime juice, walnut oil and crème fraîche in a large bowl; toss the arugula in it with salt and pepper and plate it.
Toss the citrus in the dressing left in the bowl, season, and arrange over the arugula.

i: 1 lb. asparagus, trimmed and coarsely chopped
½ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
¼ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
½ cup basil leaves, torn if large
m: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente; save ¼ cup of the water before draining.
While it cooks, pulse the raw asparagus in a food processor until finely chopped.
In a large bowl, mix the asparagus with ½ cup oil, the Parmesan, basil and lemon juice; season.
Add the hot pasta and saved water and toss until coated.
Season again, drizzle with more oil and serve.

i: One 14-oz. package firm tofu, drained and sliced 1 inch thick
m: Stir the ginger, scallion, vinegar and ⅓ cup oil together and salt to taste.
Beat the egg in one dish and spread the panko on a plate.
Dip each tofu slice in egg, then press into the panko.
Heat the remaining ⅓ cup oil in a large nonstick skillet and fry the tofu over moderate heat, turning, about 8 minutes until crisp and golden.
Salt the tofu and serve with the ginger dressing.

i: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
4 Persian or Kirby cucumbers, quartered lengthwise
1 small eggplant, halved lengthwise and cut into wedges
Leaves from 1 small bunch of basil
m: Heat a grill or grill pan.
Whisk ¼ cup oil, the vinegar, garlic and anchovies with salt and pepper.
Coat the cucumbers and eggplant with 3 Tbsp of this dressing.
Oil the grate and grill the vegetables over moderate heat 3 to 5 minutes, turning, until the cucumbers are crisp-tender and the eggplant soft.
Toss the hot vegetables with the remaining dressing and the basil. Serve warm, at room temperature or chilled, with bread.

i: 1 Tbsp. fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving
½ lb. sea scallops, thinly sliced crosswise
Flaky sea salt and thinly sliced radishes, for garnish
m: Mix the ginger, chives, olive oil and lime juice, seasoning with kosher salt and pepper.
Lay the thin scallop slices on a platter.
Spoon the ginger-chive pesto over them.
Finish with flaky salt and radish slices and serve with lime wedges.

i: 1 cup finely chopped Vidalia or other sweet onion
⅓ cup plus 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar
¼ cup coarsely chopped flat-leaf parsley
½ small red onion, thinly sliced, for garnish
Buttered toast points or saltines, for serving
m: Layer half the sweet onion in a bowl, add the crab, season, and cover with the rest of the onion.
Whisk the peanut oil, ice water and ⅓ cup vinegar and pour over the crab. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Next day, mix the mayonnaise with the lemon juice, paprika and the last 1 Tbsp vinegar.
Drain the crab and fold it into the mayonnaise with the scallions and parsley.
Top with red onion slices and serve with toast points or crackers.

i: 2 dried chiles de árbol, stemmed and crumbled
7 oz. fideos or angel hair pasta, broken into 1-inch lengths (2 cups)
1 cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
½ lb. cleaned squid, bodies cut into ¼-inch-thick rings and tentacles left whole
m: Mix the parsley and almonds for a topping.
Heat the oil in a wide casserole or paella pan and cook the shallot, garlic, chiles and noodles with salt and pepper over moderately low heat about 5 minutes, until the pasta is toasted.
Add the tomato, tomato paste and saffron and stir about 3 minutes until the paste darkens a little.
Pour in the stock and clam juice, bring to a simmer and cook about 5 minutes until the noodles are al dente.
Stir in the mussels and squid, cover and cook on low 8 to 10 minutes until the mussels open; throw out any that stay shut.
Season and scatter the parsley-almond topping over before serving.

i: ½ lb. medium shrimp—shelled, deveined and halved lengthwise
½ lb. cleaned squid, bodies cut into ¼-inch-thick rings and tentacles left whole
m: Pound the anchovies, pistachios, capers, garlic and 1 Tbsp oil in a mortar to a rough paste.
Stir in the remaining 3 Tbsp oil and the lemon juice.
Boil the shrimp in salted water about 20 seconds, just until opaque, and lift into a bowl.
Boil the squid about 20 seconds until just firm, drain and add to the shrimp.
Toss the warm seafood with the pistachio dressing and serve.

i: Four 5-oz. skinless cod fillets, halved crosswise
⅓ cup finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
6 oz. shelled and deveined medium shrimp
m: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet until shimmering.
Season the cod and dust it with 1 Tbsp flour; add it to the pan with the garlic and cook over moderately high heat about 2 minutes until just golden.
Sprinkle on the remaining flour, flip the fish, and add the peas, half the parsley, the wine and the cockles.
Cook about 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until the cod is nearly done.
Tuck in the shrimp, cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes until they turn pink and the cockles open; discard any closed ones.
Sprinkle with the rest of the parsley and serve in shallow bowls.

i: One 2½-lb. whole fish, such as red snapper, cleaned and scaled
¼ cup chopped mixed herbs, such as thyme, oregano, parsley and rosemary
m: Heat the oven to 450° and set the fish on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cut three crosswise slits to the bone on each side, rub with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Tuck a lemon slice and some herbs into each slit; fill the belly with the shallot, fennel, garlic and the remaining lemon and herbs.
Roast about 20 minutes, until the flesh is opaque.
Meanwhile stir all the salsa verde ingredients together and serve it with the fish.

i: 16 large jarred grape leaves, drained and patted dry
1 cup orange or yellow grape tomatoes, halved
5 scallions, julienned, plus 2 Tbsp. minced scallion
3 serrano chiles with seeds, halved and thinly sliced
m: Heat the oven to 450° and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Lay out four overlapping grape leaves per packet. Pile on tomatoes, three-quarters of the julienned scallions and a third of the serranos; season lightly.
Set a seasoned salmon fillet on each pile and fold the leaves around it. Place seam side down on the sheet.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon is medium in the center.
For the sauce, soften the minced scallion in the butter about 2 minutes, add the vinegar and boil about 3 minutes to reduce by half.
Whisk in the cream and simmer about 2 minutes until a little thicker; add the rest of the serranos and season.
Slit open the packets, spoon on the sauce and top with the remaining scallions.

i: One 12-oz. can of beer, preferably Pabst Blue Ribbon
m: Snip down the back of each shrimp shell with scissors and pull out the vein, leaving the shell on.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan and cook the onion, garlic, rosemary and chile over moderately high heat 5 to 7 minutes until soft and beginning to brown.
Pour in the beer and simmer about 5 minutes to reduce by half.
Add the lemon halves, Old Bay and 5 cups water and bring just to a simmer.
Add the shrimp and poach gently over low heat 8 to 10 minutes until just cooked; lift everything onto a platter.
Whisk the ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice, Sriracha and Worcestershire for the sauce.
Serve the shrimp warm or at room temperature with the cocktail sauce.

i: One 1½-lb. center-cut skinless halibut fillet (1 inch thick)
1 tsp. whole black peppercorns, plus ground pepper for seasoning
4 ears of corn, kernels cut off 3, 1 cob reserved
6 oz. wax or green beans, trimmed (2 cups)
15 small cherry tomatoes (about 8 oz.), preferably on the vine
m: Simmer 1 cup water with the sugar, fennel, peppercorns, coriander and 2½ Tbsp kosher salt until dissolved; off the heat add 3 cups ice water.
Pour the cold brine over the halibut in a shallow dish and leave 25 minutes at room temperature. Pat dry and lightly season one side.
Heat the oven to 400° and lay a 12-by-32-inch sheet of parchment on a baking sheet.
Heap the corn kernels on one half, set the fish on top skinned side up, then add the beans and tomatoes.
Drizzle with oil and vinegar, scatter the herb sprigs, lay the reserved cob alongside and dot the fish with butter.
Fold the paper over, crimp the edges tightly, adding 3 Tbsp water just before sealing.
Roast 20 minutes until the fish is just opaque; open the packet at the table.

i: 2 Tbsp. chopped dill, plus more for garnish
m: Warm the anchovies in the olive oil in a small pan over moderate heat, stirring until they dissolve.
Pour the anchovy oil into a bowl and add the ham, cabbage, pickle and chopped dill; season and mix well.
Pack into a 3-cup ramekin and top with more dill.
Serve at room temperature, with toast and mustard if you like.

i: ¾ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
¾ lb. oyster mushrooms, sliced and arranged in 2-inch clusters
20 thin strips of bacon (1 lb.), halved crosswise
m: Mix the pickles, parsley and ¾ cup oil and salt to taste for the relish.
Heat a grill.
Wrap each mushroom cluster and each tomato in a half strip of bacon and thread onto skewers.
Brush with oil, salt lightly and grill over moderate heat about 8 minutes, turning, until the bacon is done and the vegetables soft.
Brush with a little relish in the final minute, then serve with lemon wedges and the rest of the relish.

i: One 11-oz. log of semifirm goat cheese, cut into 6 pieces
Toasted sliced baguette or sourdough bread, for serving
m: Lay 3 chiles in the bottom of a small bowl at least 3 inches deep.
Set the cheese pieces on top in one layer and add 3 more chiles.
Pour in oil to cover the cheese completely and crumble the last 3 chiles into it.
Cover and refrigerate at least 3 days.
Let come to room temperature and serve with toasted bread for dipping.

i: ½ Tbsp. gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes) or ½ Tbsp. crushed red pepper
⅓ cup finely chopped drained kimchi
¼ cup firm tofu, finely chopped
m: Stir the sauce ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
Combine the pork, kimchi, tofu, scallions, garlic, ginger, egg, soy sauce and salt.
Wet the edge of a wrapper, add 1 Tbsp filling, fold into a half-moon and press shut. Repeat, keeping finished dumplings covered.
Mix the cornstarch with 1 cup plus 2 Tbsp water to a thin slurry.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in an 8-inch nonstick skillet and set 10 dumplings in a tight overlapping ring; fry over moderate heat until browned underneath.
Pour in a third of the slurry, cover for 1 minute, then uncover and cook about 4 minutes until the dumplings are done and a lacy crust forms.
Flip the pancake out onto a plate and repeat twice more. Serve with the dipping sauce.

FW|goat cheese, bacon & olive quick brea.t: 35 min active; 1 hr 15 min total, plus cooling
i: 6 slices of thick-cut bacon, cut crosswise into ½-inch-wide strips
½ cup pitted kalamata olives, halved lengthwise
1 red serrano chile, seeded and minced
m: Heat the oven to 350°. Spray a 9-inch loaf pan and line the base with parchment.
Fry the bacon over moderate heat 8 to 10 minutes until crisp; drain.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, cayenne and salt in one bowl and the eggs, buttermilk, oil and mustard in another.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry just until combined.
Fold in both cheeses, the olives, bacon, scallions, chile and thyme, and spread in the pan.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes, loosen with a knife, turn out and cool completely before slicing.

i: 1 lemon, halved, plus 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
1 Tbsp. very finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
Crusty bread or bread sticks, for serving
m: Heat the oven to 325° and fill a bowl with water acidulated with some of the lemon halves' juice.
Trim each artichoke: pull off dark outer leaves, cut the rest down to 1 inch, peel the base and stem, halve and scoop out the choke.
Quarter, rub with lemon and drop into the lemon water.
In an ovenproof skillet combine the 3 Tbsp lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, thyme and bay leaf; add the drained artichokes and bring to a simmer.
Roast about 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and spotted brown.
Remove the bay leaf, add parsley, season and let cool.
Serve the artichokes and their oil with the prosciutto and bread.

i: 2 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
8 small shelled and deveined shrimp (5 oz.)
Toasted sesame seeds and toasted sesame oil, for garnish
m: Whisk the eggs with the stock, fish sauce and salt and divide among four 10-ounce heatproof bowls.
Set the bowls in two wide lidded pots and pour boiling water two-thirds of the way up their sides.
Cover and simmer gently 6 to 7 minutes, until the custards are just a little wobbly in the middle.
Add the shrimp and scallion, cover and steam about 3 minutes more until the shrimp are cooked and the custards set.
Finish with sesame seeds and a few drops of sesame oil; serve warm.

i: 1 Tbsp. canola oil, plus more for frying
Prepared cilantro chutney and tamarind chutney, for serving
m: Heat 1 Tbsp oil and toast the cumin seeds about 30 seconds; add ginger, jalapeño, coriander and cayenne for another 30 seconds.
Add the peas and ½ cup water and cook about 5 minutes until tender and nearly dry.
Cool slightly in a food processor, add cilantro and pomegranate molasses if using, and pulse to a coarse mash; salt to taste.
Wet the edges of the wrappers and spoon filling onto each.
Shape each into a cone, pinching the seam from the tip, then fold the top down and pinch closed to make a triangle.
Heat ¾ inch of oil to 350° and fry the samosas about 5 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Drain on a rack and serve with both chutneys.

i: 1 lb. Swiss chard or collard greens, stemmed and chopped (8 cups)
2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cubed and chilled
1 tsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 1 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus more for garnish
m: Heat ¼ cup oil in a big pot and cook half the garlic 1 minute; add the clams and wine and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over moderately high heat 5 to 7 minutes, pulling clams onto a tray as they open; discard any that stay closed.
Strain the broth into a blender with the roasted peppers and blend smooth.
Rinse the pot, heat the remaining ¼ cup oil and cook the rest of the garlic 1 minute.
Add the pepper flakes and the greens in batches, cooking about 3 minutes until wilted; stir in the pepper broth and season.
Boil the spaghetti until al dente, drain and add to the greens with the butter, lemon zest and juice and ½ cup cheese.
Return the clams, toss to warm through and serve in bowls with more cheese.

i: Greens from 1 big bunch of radishes (8 loosely packed cups), chopped
¾ cup roasted salted pumpkin seeds (3 oz.), plus more for garnish
1 cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus more for garnish
m: Pulse the garlic, radish greens, parsley and ¾ cup pumpkin seeds in a food processor until finely chopped.
With the motor running, stream in the olive oil; stir in 1 cup cheese and season.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, saving 1 cup of the water when you drain.
Put the pasta back in the pot with the pesto, lemon juice and ½ cup of the water.
Toss over low heat about 2 minutes, loosening with more water if needed; season.
Serve topped with extra pumpkin seeds and cheese.

i: 1 cup pearl onions—blanched, peeled (or thawed frozen) and halved
½ lb. fingerling potatoes, halved lengthwise
1 Tbsp. finely chopped peeled fresh ginger
3 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
One 15-oz. can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
m: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and brown the onions and bell pepper over moderately high heat about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, garlic, ginger and harissa and stir about 2 minutes until the harissa deepens in color.
Pour in the stock and chickpeas, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over moderately low heat 12 to 14 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the coconut milk and return to a simmer.
Stir in lemon juice, season, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with warm flatbread.

i: 1½ Tbsp. capers, drained and coarsely chopped
½ tsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 4½ Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
m: Whisk the parsley, cilantro, tarragon, capers, cornichons, garlic, both mustards and olive oil together.
Slice the cauliflower top to bottom into four ½-inch slabs and season them well.
Get the canola oil very hot in a large skillet and sear the slabs over high heat 2 to 3 minutes until browned.
Flip, pour in the wine and cook 3 to 5 minutes until it evaporates and a knife slides in easily.
Plate the cauliflower and sprinkle with lemon zest.
Stir the lemon juice and vinegar into the herb sauce, season, and spoon it over the steaks.
Whisk the vinegar, lemon juice, preserved lemon, shallot, fish sauce and sugar, then whisk in ¼ cup oil; add parsley and season.
Season the trout. Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a large skillet until shimmering.
Lay in three fillets skin down, pressing them flat, and cook over high heat about 3 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Turn and cook about 30 seconds until just opaque; drain. Wipe the pan and repeat with the remaining oil and fish.
Plate skin side up, top with watercress and spoon some vinaigrette over; pass the rest.

i: ⅓ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
Four 5-oz. arctic char or salmon fillets with skin
m: Toast the unpeeled garlic in a dry skillet over moderate heat 7 to 8 minutes until the skins blacken; cool and peel.
Blend ⅓ cup oil with the garlic, parsley, cilantro, olives, lemon juice, cumin and paprika until smooth; salt it.
Heat the remaining 2 Tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet and season the fish.
Cook skin side down over moderately high heat about 3 minutes until golden, then flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes until it just flakes.
Drain briefly and serve with the charmoula.

i: 8 fresh or frozen kaffir lime leaves
1 Tbsp. vegetable oil, plus more for rubbing
4 hot dog buns or hero rolls, split
m: Heat the oven to 300°. Boil the lobsters about 8 minutes until bright red; drain and cool.
Twist off the tails, cut open the shells and pull out the tail, claw and knuckle meat; split the tails and remove the dark vein. Chill the meat.
Tear each lime leaf off its central stem into two halves, rub with oil and bake about 8 minutes until crisp.
Soften the shallot in 1 Tbsp oil over moderately low heat about 2 minutes, mash in the anchovies, add the curry powder and cook 1 minute.
Cool this mixture, then stir in the mayonnaise, lime juice and dill; salt it and chill 15 minutes.
Fold the curry mayo through the lobster, pile into the buns and top with crisp lime leaves and cucumber.

i: 1 lb. ground chicken, preferably dark meat
½ cup cooked wheat berries or spelt
1 Tbsp. lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving
⅓ cup chopped basil, plus whole leaves for serving
m: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet.
Add the chicken with salt and pepper and cook over moderately high heat, breaking it up, 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the wheat berries, fish sauce and lime juice.
Take off the heat and mix in the chopped basil.
Serve warm with lettuce cups, lime wedges and basil leaves for wrapping.

i: ½ lb. sourdough bread, torn into bite-size pieces
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
m: Heat the oven to 400°.
On a big rimmed sheet, toss the bread, shallots, caperberries and lemon pieces with ¼ cup oil, salt and pepper.
Brush the chicken legs with oil, season, and set them on top of the bread.
Roast about 50 minutes, until the bread is crisp and the thighs read 160°.
Serve the chicken with the toasted bread and vegetables.

i: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves (2 lbs.), pounded ¼ inch thick
1 cup finely chopped mixed herbs, such as parsley, tarragon, basil, thyme, rosemary, sage and mint
m: Season the flattened breasts, roll each up tightly lengthwise and pin with toothpicks every inch.
Bring the vinegar, ¾ cup water and a pinch of salt to a gentle simmer.
Poach the rolls over low heat 10 to 12 minutes until just white throughout; cool slightly.
Pull out the toothpicks and cut into 1-inch rounds.
Whisk the olive oil with the herbs, salt and pepper and turn the chicken in it.
Cool 30 minutes, then refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight.
Bring back to room temperature and serve with bread.

i: 3 thinly sliced scallions, plus more for garnish
4 smoked trout fillets (12 oz.), skinned, meat flaked into large pieces
Pickled radishes and rye crackers, for serving
m: Stir together the labneh, shallot, olive oil, caraway and the 3 scallions; season.
Fold in the trout gently so it stays in chunks.
Top with more scallions.
Serve at room temperature with pickled radishes and rye crackers.

i: 1¼ lbs. mixed tender mushrooms, such as maitake, oyster and enoki, cut into small pieces
½ lb. Italian Fontina cheese, shredded (about 1 cup)
m: Bake the potatoes on a sheet at 450° for 1 hour, until tender.
Meanwhile melt 1 Tbsp butter with the oil and cook the mushrooms over moderately high heat about 5 minutes until golden; season.
Cut each potato open lengthwise halfway down and add 1 Tbsp butter and 2 Tbsp cheese; salt it.
Pile on the mushrooms and the rest of the cheese.
Bake about 3 minutes to melt the cheese, sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

i: 3 celery ribs, cut into ½-inch pieces
2 qts. chicken stock or low-sodium broth
4 cups bite-size pieces of roast chicken or turkey
m: Melt the butter in a large saucepan and cook the celery, carrots, onion, garlic and thyme with salt and pepper over moderate heat about 10 minutes until starting to soften.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir about 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the wild rice, then slowly stir in the stock and 2 cups water; bring to a boil.
Simmer over moderately low heat about 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Add the chicken and simmer 10 to 15 minutes more until the rice is tender.
Stir in the cream, season and serve.

i: 3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
½ lb. all-butter puff pastry, cut in half
½ lb. thinly sliced baked ham
1 large egg yolk mixed with 1 tsp. water
m: Melt the butter and cook the shallot over moderate heat 3 to 5 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and boil gently 5 to 7 minutes, whisking, until thick.
Add mustard and nutmeg, season and let the sauce cool.
Roll each pastry half to 10 by 6 inches; put one on a parchment-lined sheet.
Leaving a 1-inch border, layer a third of the sauce, half the cheese and half the ham; repeat, then finish with the last of the sauce.
Cover with the second sheet, press and crimp the edges, cut four small slits and brush with egg wash. Chill about 20 minutes.
Bake at 450° for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

i: ¾ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus shavings for garnish
3 firm, fresh medium zucchini and/or yellow squash (1¼ lbs.), very thinly sliced lengthwise on a mandoline
m: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over moderately low heat about 5 minutes; chop ½ cup finely and the rest coarsely.
Pulse 2 cups arugula in a food processor until fine and transfer to a big bowl.
Stir in ¾ cup oil, the garlic, grated cheese and finely chopped walnuts; season.
Cook the pappardelle in salted water until al dente, drain and toss with the pesto and squash ribbons.
Add the lemon juice and remaining arugula and season.
Drizzle with oil and top with the coarse walnuts and cheese shavings.

i: 2 small leeks, white and tender green parts only, thinly sliced (2 cups)
4 cups chopped mustard or turnip greens
2 dozen oysters, freshly shucked, with their liquor
m: Melt 2 Tbsp butter in a large enameled casserole and cook the leeks with salt over moderate heat about 8 minutes until soft.
Add the greens, thyme, garlic and pepper flakes and stir about 2 minutes until wilted.
Pour in the vermouth, add the clams, boil, then cover and cook 5 to 10 minutes, removing clams as they open; discard any that don't.
Add the oysters with their liquor, the cream, parsley, lemon juice, hot sauce and remaining butter.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes just until the oyster edges curl; remove the thyme.
Return the clams and their juices and serve right away with bread.

i: ½ cup plus 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for greasing
2 spring onions or 6 scallions, thinly sliced
1 tsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 2 tsp. fresh lemon juice
4 oz. country white bread, crusts removed and bread torn into ½-inch pieces (2 cups)
m: Heat the oven to 450°. Spread the eggplant over 2 baking sheets, coat with 6 Tbsp of the oil, season and roast 10 minutes.
Toss the spring onions with 2 Tbsp oil, add them to the eggplant with the butter and roast 15 minutes more, stirring, until tender.
Mix the ricotta with the cream, lemon zest and juice and parsley; season. Toss the bread with the last 1 Tbsp oil.
Spoon the eggplant and onions into a greased 2-quart baking dish, dollop with the ricotta and scatter the bread on top.
Bake about 10 minutes until the bread is golden.
Prep ahead: the roasted eggplant keeps overnight in the fridge; bring to room temperature before finishing.

i: 1 tsp. fresh lemon juice, plus wedges for serving
1 lb. jumbo lump crabmeat, picked over for shells
m: Set the broiler to its lowest setting with a rack 12 inches below it; butter a small rimmed baking sheet with 1 Tbsp of the butter.
Whisk the egg with the mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt, pepper and cayenne, then gently fold in the crab and ¼ cup of the breadcrumbs. Chill 10 minutes.
Pack a quarter of the mix into a ½-cup measure, turn it out onto the sheet and shape into a loose patty with damp hands; repeat to make 4.
Scatter the remaining ¼ cup breadcrumbs over the cakes.
Broil 5 minutes until golden, pour the rest of the butter over and broil 1 minute more.
Lift onto plates with a wide spatula and serve with lemon wedges.

i: 2 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, plus wedges for serving
Four 1½-lb. lobsters, halved lengthwise, claws detached and reserved
m: Melt the butter and whisk in the miso, Sriracha and lemon juice; set aside ¼ cup for the table.
Light the grill. Oil and season the scallions, grill about 5 minutes until charred and tender, then chop and toss with 1 Tbsp of the miso butter.
Run a skewer through each lobster half from tail to head so it stays flat; brush the meat with 2 Tbsp miso butter.
Cook the bodies and claws on the grill at moderate heat, turning them and brushing on the rest of the butter: 7 to 8 minutes for tails, 12 to 15 for claws.
Pull out the skewers, pile the lobsters on a platter with the scallions on top and serve with lemon wedges and the reserved butter.

i: 1 medium zucchini, very thinly sliced lengthwise on a mandoline
m: Pulse the parsley, garlic, crushed red pepper and oil in a blender to a thick puree; season.
Thread each skewer with alternating bay leaf, swordfish, bay leaf and zucchini ribbon so each ends up with 3 pieces of fish, 3 zucchini slices and 7 bay leaves.
Season the skewers, brush all over with the parsley sauce and refrigerate 1 hour.
Grill over moderate heat, turning, about 6 minutes until the fish is browned and cooked through.
Grill the lemon halves cut side down about 2 minutes until charred.
Serve the skewers with the grilled lemons, discarding the bay leaves.

i: Four 7-oz. sea bass or red snapper fillets with skin
One 1½-inch piece of fresh ginger, peeled and cut into very thin matchsticks
Finely grated zest and juice of 1 lime
4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
Chopped cilantro leaves and sliced scallion, for garnish
m: Slash the skin of each fillet 4 times and lay them skin side up in a large glass or ceramic pie plate.
Scatter over the ginger, chile, garlic and lime zest, season, dot with the butter and pour on the lime juice.
Put 3 balls of foil in a very large deep skillet, add 1 inch of water and bring to a boil.
Rest the pie plate on the foil, cover tightly and steam about 5 minutes until the fish flakes.
Move the fillets to shallow bowls, spoon over the buttery juices and top with cilantro and scallion.

i: Four 6-oz. red snapper (or other white fish) fillets with skin
Lemon wedges and greens, for serving
m: Stir the dried herbs, cayenne and turmeric into the flour in a shallow bowl.
Season the fillets and coat them in the spiced flour.
Heat the oil in a large cast-iron skillet until shimmering.
Lay the fish in skin side down, press flat with a spatula and cook over moderately high heat about 4 minutes until the skin browns.
Flip and cook about 2 minutes more until opaque throughout; serve with lemon wedges and greens.

i: 1 lb. thinly sliced roast turkey breast
One 6½-oz. can tuna in water, drained
½ cup chopped mixed herbs, such as tarragon, chives and dill
m: Lay the turkey slices out on a platter.
Blend the tuna, chickpeas and yogurt in a food processor.
With the motor running, pour in the oil until the sauce is smooth.
Add the capers and chopped herbs, then season.
Spoon the sauce over the turkey and serve.
Heat the oven to 375° and set the ham in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
