Simmer everything else together in a small saucepan over moderately low heat about 25 minutes, until reduced to ¾ cup.
Pour the glaze over the ham, spices and all, cover tightly with foil and bake about 1 hour 15 minutes, basting every 15 minutes, until hot through.
Move the ham to a platter and strain the pan juices into a small saucepan.
Boil the juices 8 to 10 minutes to a glaze and spoon over the ham.
Prep ahead: the glaze can be made 2 days in advance and refrigerated; rewarm before using.

i: 1 tsp. dried summer savory or dried oregano
2 medium carrots, sliced diagonally 1 inch thick
¼ head of cauliflower, cut into 1½-inch florets
¼ lb. haricots verts or thin green beans
4 boneless chicken breast halves with skin
¼ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Grind the coriander, mustard seeds, peppercorns and savory to a powder.

Steam the vegetables in layers (potatoes, carrots, cauliflower, beans) over 1 inch of simmering water, lifting out the beans after about 3 minutes, the cauliflower 3 minutes later and the carrots and potatoes after 10 minutes more.
Toss the vegetables in 2 Tbsp butter over moderately high heat about 1 minute, add the lemon juice and season.

Season the chicken and coat with the ground spices. Cook skin side down in the remaining 3 Tbsp butter over moderately low heat about 12 minutes until deeply browned, then turn and cook, basting, about 7 minutes more.
Rewarm the vegetables. Boil the stock in the chicken skillet 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, then boil in the crème fraîche, take off the heat and stir in the tarragon; season.
Sauce the chicken and serve with the vegetables alongside.
Prep ahead: the spice mix and steamed vegetables can be done a day in advance.

i: One 4-lb. chicken, backbone removed, chicken halved lengthwise
1 cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
m: Heat the oven to 450°. Set the chicken halves skin side up on a rack over a baking sheet, rub with 2 Tbsp oil and season.
Put the lemon halves cut side down on the rack and roast about 40 minutes until the chicken is golden and cooked through; rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile pound the capers, anchovies and garlic to a paste in a mortar or blender.
Whisk the remaining 1 cup oil into the paste, stir in all the herbs and salt to taste.
Carve the chicken, arrange with the roasted lemons and serve with the salsa verde (it can be made the night before and served at room temperature).
Bring the rice, coconut milk, sugar and ½ tsp salt to a boil in a large saucepan.
Cover and cook over low heat about 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Let the rice stand off the heat for 10 minutes.
Tip into a bowl and fold through the chicken, cucumber and oil.
Season with salt, top with scallions and serve.

i: 2½ Tbsp. red hot sauce, preferably Frank's RedHot
m: Heat the oven to 500° and line a large baking sheet with foil coated in cooking spray.
Mix the flour, salt, paprika, dried garlic and onion in a large bowl and toss the wings through it.
Spread the wings on the sheet, mist with spray and roast 45 minutes, turning once or twice, until crisp and browned.
Whisk the hot sauce with the melted butter and pepper jelly in a large bowl.
Toss the hot wings in the glaze and serve.

i: 6 oz. thick-sliced bacon, cut crosswise into ⅓-inch lardons
3 oz. Brie, thinly sliced (with rind, if desired)
m: Put a pizza stone in the oven and heat to 500°. Bake the bacon in a pie plate 15 minutes, stirring once, until almost crisp; drain.

Beat the eggs with the cream and a little salt, then cook with 1 Tbsp butter in a nonstick skillet over low heat, whisking often, about 12 minutes to a creamy small curd. Off the heat stir in the other 1 Tbsp butter and salt.
Stretch the dough to a 12-inch round on a floured peel, spread with crème fraîche leaving a 1-inch rim, and top with the bacon, Brie and mozzarella.
Bake on the stone about 7 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Spoon the scrambled eggs over, return to the stone about 2 minutes until hot, scatter with chives and cut into wedges.

i: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil
1 lb. shelled and deveined medium shrimp
3 oz. sliced mixed wild mushrooms (1 packed cup)
3 scallions, halved lengthwise and cut into 1-inch lengths
1 Tbsp. hoisin sauce, plus more for serving
m: Warm the tortillas wrapped in foil in a 200° oven.
Get a wok very hot, add 1 Tbsp oil until smoking and stir-fry the shrimp about 2 minutes until just cooked; move to a platter.
Add 2 Tbsp oil, pour in the seasoned eggs and stir about 2 minutes to soft curds; add to the shrimp.
Stir-fry the ginger, garlic and mushrooms in 2 Tbsp oil about 4 minutes until browned.
Add the last 1 Tbsp oil with the coleslaw mix and scallions, season and stir-fry about 4 minutes until the cabbage just wilts.
Return the shrimp and eggs, toss with 1 Tbsp hoisin and serve with the tortillas, cilantro and extra hoisin.

i: ½ cup finely shredded green cabbage
½ cup thinly sliced yellow onion (½ small)
½ cup julienned taro or potato
Chinese hot mustard and/or sweet chile sauce, for dipping
m: Boil the noodles 4 to 5 minutes until al dente, chill in ice water, drain and cut into 3-inch lengths.
Combine the noodles with the pork, carrots, cabbage, onion, taro, oyster sauce, salt, sugar and pepper.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a large casserole to 350°.
Set a wrapper with a corner toward you, put ¼ cup filling in the lower third, roll up tucking in the sides and seal the tip with beaten egg; repeat, keeping the wrappers under a damp towel.
Fry the rolls about 5 minutes, turning, until golden and the pork is cooked; drain on paper towels.
Serve with hot mustard and/or sweet chile sauce. Unfried rolls can be refrigerated up to 4 hours under a damp cloth.

i: 7 oz. firm tofu, cubed and dried
½ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
1 tsp. black soy sauce or ¾ tsp. soy sauce sweetened with ¼ tsp. molasses
½ red bell pepper, seeded and sliced
½ large jalapeño, seeded and sliced
½ lb. pad thai rice noodles, cooked and cut in half crosswise
1 cup Thai basil leaves, plus more for garnish
m: Fry the tofu in ¼ inch of oil over moderately high heat about 5 minutes, turning, until crisp; drain.
Stir the stock with the oyster, fish and soy sauces, the chile paste and the sugar.
Stir-fry the bell pepper, jalapeño, garlic and Thai chile in 2 Tbsp oil over high heat about 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and stir-fry about 4 minutes until browned.
Add the sauce and keep tossing over moderately high heat until it is soaked up, then mix in the basil and tofu.
Top with extra basil leaves and put lime wedges alongside.

i: 5 Tbsp. Asian fish sauce (nuoc mam or nam pla)
1 lb. skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut lengthwise into 12 strips
12 long wooden skewers, soaked in water for 1 hour
2 Tbsp. plus 1 tsp. fresh lime juice (from about 2 limes)
1 cucumber—peeled, halved lengthwise, seeded and thinly sliced
⅔ cup mint, basil or cilantro leaves, or any combination of these
m: Heat the broiler or grill. Toss the chicken strips with 1 Tbsp fish sauce, 1 Tbsp sugar, 2 of the garlic cloves and the oil, thread onto skewers and cook about 2 minutes per side.
For the nuoc cham, mix the other 4 Tbsp fish sauce, 1 Tbsp sugar and last garlic clove with the chile flakes, vinegar, lime juice and 2 Tbsp water.
Boil the vermicelli in salted water about 9 minutes, adding the bean sprouts for the final minute; drain, rinse cold and drain well.
Spread the noodles and sprouts on a platter and top with cucumber, herbs and the skewers.
Pour over the nuoc cham, scatter with peanuts and serve.

i: ⅓ cup minced peeled fresh ginger
4 chicken legs, cut into drumsticks and thighs
m: Heat the oven to 400°. Make a marinade of the vinegar, honey, ginger, jalapeño, all the spices, salt, pepper and 3 tsp of the lime zest.
Prick the chicken all over with a fork and toss it in the marinade. Mix the sugar with the remaining ½ tsp zest.
Brown the chicken in 2 Tbsp butter and the oil in a large ovenproof skillet over moderately high heat about 5 minutes, turning.
Sprinkle with the lime sugar and roast 25 minutes until cooked through.
Stir the lime juice and remaining 2 Tbsp butter into the pan juices and serve with lime wedges, plus rice or naan.

i: 1½ cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Heat the oven to 300°. Season the chicken and brown it in two batches in 2 Tbsp canola oil, about 8 minutes a batch; pour off the fat and wipe the pot.
Soften the onion, carrot, celery and shallots in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil about 8 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the Riesling, simmer 1 minute scraping the pot, then pour in the stock, add the thyme and bring up to a boil.
Tuck in the chicken, cover and braise in the oven 1 hour until tender.
Meanwhile brown the mushrooms in the butter and olive oil over high heat about 5 minutes without stirring, then season and cook 3 to 5 minutes more.
Lift out the chicken, strain and skim the braising liquid and boil it down to 1½ cups; whisk in the crème fraîche and lemon juice and season.
Return the chicken and mushrooms to the sauce, simmer 3 minutes and finish with tarragon.

i: ½ small kabocha squash (1 lb.)—peeled, seeded and cut into 1½-inch pieces (4 cups)
½ cup chopped mixed herbs, such as cilantro and basil
m: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and fry the curry paste with the squash over high heat about 3 minutes until lightly caramelized.
Add 4 cups water with the coconut milk and fish sauce and bring up to a boil.
Cover and simmer about 15 minutes until the squash is tender.
Finish with the turkey, lime juice and herbs, check the seasoning and serve.

i: ¾ lb. green beans, thinly sliced crosswise
7 to 10 dried Chinese hot red chiles, cracked
m: Heat the oil in a large skillet until shimmering.
Brown the pork over moderately high heat, breaking it up, about 5 minutes until nearly done.
Add the green beans, chiles and garlic and stir-fry over high heat about 7 minutes until the beans are crisp-tender.
Season with the soy sauce, lime juice, salt and white pepper.
Serve over steamed rice.

i: 2 Granny Smith apples—peeled, cored and thinly sliced
Eight ½-inch-thick hand-cut slices from a loaf of white bread
½ lb. thickly sliced smoked ham
m: Simmer the apples with the maple syrup, cinnamon stick and 1 cup water about 6 minutes until tender; lift out and cool.
Whisk the milk and eggs in a shallow bowl. Spread 4 bread slices with mustard and layer on half the cheese, the ham and the rest of the cheese.
Melt 1 Tbsp butter in a large skillet over low heat. Dip the bottoms of the topped slices in the egg and set them in the pan; dip the lids on one side only and put them soaked side up.
Cover and cook over moderately low heat about 3 minutes until browned underneath, flip (adding butter if needed), cover and cook about 3 minutes more until the cheese melts.
Rest 5 minutes, halve and serve with the maple apples and some steamed greens.

i: 1 lb. mixed sausages, such as bratwurst and fresh chorizo
1 lb. small Yukon Gold potatoes, quartered
One 25-oz. jar of sauerkraut, drained (3 cups)
Crusty bread and grainy mustard, for serving
m: Heat the oven to 425°.
Toss the sausages, potatoes, sauerkraut, oil and caraway in a large cast-iron skillet and season.
Roast about 45 minutes until the potatoes are golden and cooked through.
Serve with crusty bread and grainy mustard.

i: 1 tsp. finely grated lime zest plus 2 Tbsp. fresh lime juice
1 head of butter lettuce (6 oz.), leaves separated
m: Soften the onion in the oil over moderate heat about 5 minutes until golden, then cook the garlic 1 minute.
Add the pork and brown about 3 minutes, breaking it up.
Season with the honey, fish sauce and sesame oil and give it 2 more minutes until the pork is fully cooked.
Off the heat add the lime zest and juice and season.
Spoon into lettuce leaves, top with scallions and serve with lime wedges.

i: ⅓ cup Thai red curry paste
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. finely grated palm sugar or dark brown sugar
One 4-lb. boneless pork shoulder roast with fat cap
1 stalk of fresh lemongrass, inner light green and white parts only, cut into 3 pieces
One ½-inch piece of fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
One 15-oz. can unsweetened coconut milk, chilled
⅓ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
½ cup each finely chopped cilantro, Thai basil and mint leaves
Thinly sliced cucumber and red onion, cilantro, Thai basil and lime wedges, for serving
m: Heat the oven to 325°. Warm the curry paste, fish sauce and ¼ cup of palm sugar together, stirring, until smooth; cool a little.
Salt the pork, rub it with the paste, and roast covered in a large casserole about 3½ hours until very tender, basting now and then; uncover for the last 15 minutes to crust.
Rest 15 minutes, shred with forks and stir the skimmed pan juices back through; keep warm.

Seal the cilantro stems and all the remaining aromatics and spices (garlic through turmeric) in a double foil packet and set it on a burner or hot cast-iron pan about 5 minutes until smoky and lightly charred inside.
Process the packet contents with the remaining 2 Tbsp palm sugar to a paste.
Simmer the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk, whisk in the paste, then the rest of the coconut milk and the stock.
Stir in the pork, season and simmer about 10 minutes to thicken; add the chopped herbs.
Pile onto mayonnaise-spread buns with cucumber, red onion, cilantro and basil and serve with lime wedges.

i: 1 lb. seedless watermelon, cut into 1-inch cubes (from one 3¼-lb. watermelon)
2 Kirby cucumbers, peeled and cut into ¾-inch dice
¼ cup very thinly sliced red onion
½ tsp. gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes) or Aleppo pepper
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
m: In a large baking dish gently combine the watermelon, cucumbers, onion, vinegar, gochugaru and ¼ cup of the oil; spread out and season.
Sear the shishitos in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil over high heat about 2 minutes until blistered and crisp-tender.
Toss the peppers through the watermelon.
Plate and finish with the olives, feta, watercress, cilantro and dill; eat straight away.
Warm the oil in a large skillet and cook the garlic, orange zest and crushed red pepper over moderate heat about 2 minutes until the garlic softens.
Add the olives and heat through about 5 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat and stir in the orange juice.
Cool completely, stirring occasionally, and serve at room temperature.

i: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. heavy cream
4 oz. smoked sablefish, sliced ¼ inch thick
Trout roe, thinly sliced scallions and sour cream, for garnish
Toasted sesame, everything or plain bagels, for serving
m: Put the eggs, cream and ½ Tbsp of the butter in a medium nonstick skillet.
Cook over moderately low heat, whisking constantly, 5 to 7 minutes until small creamy curds form; remove from the heat.
Fold in the remaining ½ Tbsp butter and a little salt.
Divide between 2 bowls, lay the sablefish on top and garnish with trout roe, scallions and sour cream.
Serve at once with toasted bagels (smoked salmon and salmon roe can stand in).

i: 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, plus softened butter for brushing
¼ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
2 leeks, white parts only, thinly sliced
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. all-purpose flour
m: Heat the oven to 400°. Butter eight 1-cup ramekins, dust with 2 Tbsp of the Parmigiano and set on a sturdy baking sheet.
Wilt the leeks in 2 Tbsp butter over high heat about 5 minutes; set aside and wipe the pan.
Make a thick white sauce: melt the remaining 4 Tbsp butter, cook the flour 1 minute, whisk in the milk and cook about 2 minutes until very thick; add the salt and cayenne.
Off the heat whisk in the yolks, cool slightly, then stir in the Gouda, ham and leeks in a large bowl.
Beat the whites with the cream of tartar to firm peaks and fold into the base until no streaks remain.

Fill the ramekins to ½ inch below the rim, run a thumb round the inside edge, top with the last 2 Tbsp Parmigiano and bake in the lower third of the oven 20 minutes until puffed and golden; serve at once.
Variation: bake in one 8-cup soufflé dish at 375° for 40 minutes. The yolk base can be made the night before.

i: ¾ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
3 medium tomatoes, seeded and cut into ½-inch dice (2 cups)
One 12-oz. eggplant, seeds removed and flesh cut into ½-inch dice (2 cups)
2 small zucchini, cut into ½-inch dice (2 cups)
2 large red onions, cut into ½-inch dice
1 red bell pepper, cut into ½-inch dice
1 cup chopped basil, plus more for garnish
Six ½-inch-thick slices of sourdough bread, toasted
m: Cook the tomatoes in 2 Tbsp oil with 1 garlic clove, ¼ tsp crushed red pepper and salt over moderate heat about 5 minutes until just soft; tip into a saucepan, discarding the garlic.

Cook the eggplant, zucchini, onions and bell pepper the same way, one vegetable at a time, each with 2 Tbsp oil, a garlic clove, ¼ tsp crushed red pepper and salt, about 7 minutes each, adding each to the saucepan.
Add the bay leaf, ½ cup basil and ⅓ cup water, cover and cook over moderately low heat about 20 minutes until very tender.
Discard the bay leaf, stir in the remaining ½ cup basil, season and cool a little.
Fry the eggs in the last 2 Tbsp oil in two batches of 3, 3 to 5 minutes, until the whites set and the yolks stay runny; season.
Spoon ratatouille onto the toasts, top each with an egg, and finish with a drizzle of oil and basil. The ratatouille keeps 3 days in the fridge.

i: 4 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for greasing
m: Mix the flour, sugar and yeast in a stand mixer with the dough hook, then work in half the warm water, the 3 Tbsp oil and the salt, followed by the rest of the water, until a ball forms; knead 2 minutes low, 2 medium, 2 low.
Rise the dough in an oiled, covered bowl about 1½ hours until doubled.
Heat a pizza stone on the oven floor at 500° for about 45 minutes.
Punch down the dough, divide into 8 balls, flatten into disks and rest covered 20 minutes.
Simmer the sun-dried tomatoes in water about 5 minutes until soft, drain and chop; puree the garlic with the ⅓ cup oil.
Roll or stretch a disk to an 8-inch round on a floured peel, brush with garlic oil, scatter with an eighth of the tomatoes and cheese, drizzle with more garlic oil and season.
Bake on the stone about 4 minutes until crisp and bubbling, top with arugula and serve; repeat with the rest.
Prep ahead: the punched-down dough, tomatoes and garlic oil can all be refrigerated overnight.

i: Four 12-oz. dorade—scaled, cleaned and patted dry
5 dried Turkish figs, stemmed and quartered
½ cup each pitted Cerignola and Castelvetrano olives
m: Heat the oven to 350° and slick a large roasting pan with 1 Tbsp of the oil.
Lay in the dorade and salt them well.
Strew the figs, olives, rosemary and almonds around and over the fish, then pour on the wine and the remaining 3 Tbsp oil.
Roast about 30 minutes until the flesh just flakes and serve with lemon wedges.

i: 1 Tbsp. salted capers, rinsed and minced
Sliced tomatoes and arugula, for serving
m: Spread the tuna, scallion, olive and caper mixture on a plate and firm it up in the freezer 5 minutes.
Pulse the mixture in a food processor until finely chopped, season and shape into four 4-inch patties.
Brush the burgers with oil and grill over moderately high heat about 6 minutes, turning once, until crusty and just cooked through.
Stir the anchovy paste into the mayonnaise and spread on the buns.
Add the burgers, tomato and arugula and serve.

i: 1 medium fennel bulb, shaved paper-thin, plus 2 Tbsp. chopped fronds
1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
¼ cup finely chopped red onion
¼ cup pitted niçoise olives, chopped
Two 6-oz. jars tuna packed in olive oil, drained and flaked
m: Toast the fennel seeds about 3 minutes until golden and crush them in a mortar.
Puree the crushed seeds into the mayonnaise and crème fraîche with the garlic, fennel fronds, 2 tsp zest and 1 Tbsp lemon juice; season.
Mix the onion with the olives, capers, chile flakes and the remaining zest and juice, then fold in the tuna and olive oil.
Spread the fennel mayo over both cut sides of the baguette.
Layer arugula, shaved fennel and the tuna on the base, then tomatoes, cucumber and anchovies.
Close, cut into 4 and serve; wrapped in parchment the sandwiches keep 4 hours in the fridge, the mayo 3 days.

i: 1 lb. large shrimp, shelled and deveined
½ lb. baby squid, bodies cut into ¼-inch rings
m: Sear the seasoned shrimp on one side in the hot oil in a large deep skillet about 2 minutes; set aside.
Toast the rice in the skillet about 2 minutes until opaque, then stir in the tomato paste, paprika, garlic and saffron for 1 minute.
Add the clam juice and 2 cups water, bring to a boil and boil about 10 minutes until half the liquid is absorbed.
Lower the heat and simmer about 8 minutes until the rice is nearly tender and still soupy.
Stir in the squid, lay the shrimp on top cooked side up, cover and simmer about 2 minutes more until everything is cooked through.

i: ¾ lb. potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
5 oz. cured Spanish chorizo, cut into ½-inch dice
m: Boil a large pan of salted water with the onion and bay leaves; dip the octopus in 3 times, then leave it to cook over moderately low heat about 1 hour until tender.
Rest the octopus in the water 10 minutes off the heat, drain and cut into ½-inch pieces.
Boil the potatoes in salted water about 10 minutes until just tender, drain and toss with the 3 Tbsp oil and thyme; season.
Warm the chorizo in a grill pan about 2 minutes and move to a large bowl.
Cook the potatoes and octopus in the same pan about 5 minutes until hot and golden in spots.
Toss with the chorizo, season, drizzle with oil and add shiso if you like.

i: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
1½ lbs. skinless salmon fillet, cut into 1½-inch cubes
4 long metal skewers, or 4 wooden skewers soaked in water for 1 hour
m: Whisk the ¼ cup oil with the lemon juice, mustard and rosemary and season the vinaigrette.
Heat a grill or grill pan and thread the salmon and tomatoes onto the skewers.
Brush with oil, season all over and grill over moderately high heat about 6 minutes, turning once, until the salmon is just cooked.
Drizzle the skewers with some vinaigrette and pass the rest at the table.
Rub the chicken pieces with the garlic and 1 Tbsp salt and refrigerate, covered, for 1 hour.
Scrape off the garlic and brown the chicken in the oil in a large deep skillet over moderately high heat about 12 minutes; set aside.
Cook the onion in the pan over low heat about 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the piquillos and wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the chicken with its juices, partly cover and cook over low heat about 30 minutes until tender and the sauce has thickened.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken to serve; it reheats well the next day.

i: ½ lb. smoked duck breast—skin and fat removed and reserved, breast thinly sliced crosswise
6 oz. frisée, torn into bite-size pieces (6 cups)
m: Heat the oven to 350°. Bake the reserved duck skin and fat in a pie plate about 15 minutes until crisp; drain and break into cracklings.
Toast the walnuts in the oven about 8 minutes, cool and chop coarsely.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard and shallot, then slowly whisk in the walnut and vegetable oils; season well.
Toss the frisée, Boston lettuce and walnuts in the dressing.
Top with raspberries, sliced duck and cracklings and serve.

i: 2 medium peaches, pitted and sliced ¼ inch thick
m: Shake both vinegars with the sorghum, salt and ½ cup water in a jar until the salt dissolves.
Add the jalapeños and onion and leave at room temperature at least 1 hour.
Grill the sausages over moderate heat on an oiled grate, turning, 10 to 12 minutes until charred and cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly on the diagonal.
Lay the peach slices on a platter, pile on the sausages and some pickles, drizzle with pickling liquid and pass the rest of the pickles.

i: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
1 small onion, cut into ¼-inch dice
2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into ¼-inch dice
1 baby eggplant (8 oz.), peeled and cut into ¼-inch dice
1 lb. cremini mushrooms, one-fourth sliced, the rest cut into ¼-inch dice
8 oz. shiitake mushrooms, stemmed, caps cut into ¼-inch dice
One 2-inch chunk of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus grated cheese for serving
One 28-oz. can whole peeled tomatoes, crushed
m: Soak the porcini in 1 cup boiling water about 30 minutes; chop finely and keep ½ cup of the liquid.
Cook the onion and carrots in 2 Tbsp oil in a large casserole about 8 minutes until light golden, then add the eggplant with 2 Tbsp more oil and cook 8 minutes.
Add all the mushrooms and the last 2 Tbsp oil, season, and cook 8 to 10 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and miso for 2 minutes, then add the cheese chunk, tomatoes, thyme, sugar and soaking liquid.
Cover and simmer over low heat about 1½ hours until very thick; discard the thyme and season.
Boil the spaghetti until al dente, keeping ¼ cup of the water.
Toss the pasta, water and parsley with the sauce and serve with grated cheese.

i: 2 leeks, white and tender green parts only, thinly sliced
¼ lb. shiitake mushrooms, stemmed, caps thinly sliced
3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour, plus more for coating
¼ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
2 large eggs beaten with 2 Tbsp. water
m: Cook the leeks and shiitake in 2 Tbsp butter over high heat about 7 minutes until soft and browning; season, add the herbs and tip into a bowl.
Make a thick white sauce with the remaining 3 Tbsp butter, 3 Tbsp flour and the milk, cooking about 3 minutes; stir it into the vegetables with both cheeses and season.
Spoon the mixture onto plastic wrap, roll into a 14-inch log and freeze about 2 hours until firm.
Cut the log into 12 pieces and pat each into a 2-inch patty with floured hands.
Coat each in flour, egg and panko, then freeze 15 minutes.
Fry in ½ inch of 375° oil about 5 minutes, turning, until golden; drain and serve hot.

i: 3 very large carrots, cut crosswise 1 inch thick at the wide ends and 1½ inches thick toward the narrow ends
1 Tbsp. porcini mushroom powder (ground dried porcini mushrooms)
m: Heat the oven to 350°. Blanch the pearl onions 1 minute in a deep ovenproof skillet, then trim and peel them.
Brown the carrot pieces in 1 Tbsp oil over moderate heat, seasoned, about 5 minutes a side.
Add the onions and curry powder for 1 minute, pour in the wine and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the porcini powder and broth, bring to a boil and braise in the oven 1 hour 15 minutes, turning once, until tender.
Season the sauce and spoon carrots, onions and sauce into bowls.
Toss the parsley with lemon juice and the last 1 tsp oil, season and scatter over. Good with soft polenta or celery root puree.

i: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
¾ lb. medium shells, such as Barilla
2½ lbs. cauliflower, cut into small florets (1 large head)
3 Tbsp. roughly chopped fresh sage leaves
¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
2 cups freshly grated Italian Fontina Val d'Aosta cheese, lightly packed (10 oz. with rind)
6 Tbsp. freshly grated Italian Pecorino cheese
m: Heat the oven to 400°. Boil the shells in well-salted water just to al dente, drain and put in a very large bowl.
Sauté the cauliflower in two batches in 3 Tbsp olive oil each over medium-high heat, 5 to 6 minutes per batch, until browned and tender; add to the pasta.
Stir in the sage, capers, garlic, lemon zest, pepper flakes, 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper, then the Fontina.
Spread half the mixture in a 10 x 13-inch baking dish, dot with spoonfuls of ricotta and cover with the rest.
Mix the panko, Pecorino, parsley and 1 Tbsp oil and scatter on top.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until browned and crusty. Can be assembled a day ahead and baked before serving.

i: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
3 cups French green du Puy lentils (20 oz.), rinsed and picked over
Greek yogurt, chopped walnuts and parsley, small mint leaves and pomegranate molasses, for serving
m: Soften the onion, celery, garlic and bay leaf in 2 Tbsp oil over moderate heat.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer about 45 minutes until the lentils are tender but intact; remove the bay leaf.
Meanwhile rub the eggplants with the remaining oil and broil 6 inches from the heat about 20 minutes, turning, until blackened and soft.
Halve the eggplants, scoop the flesh into a colander to drain 5 minutes, then mash smooth.
Stir the harissa and half the eggplant into the lentils, add the parsley and season.
Serve topped with the rest of the eggplant, yogurt, walnuts, parsley, mint, pomegranate molasses and a drizzle of oil.

FW|poulet basquaise with currant couscou.t: 1 hr 15 min active; 2 hr 30 min total
i: 6 whole chicken legs, separated into thighs and drumsticks
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
m: Heat the oven to 350°. Season the chicken and brown it in the oil in a large casserole in two batches, about 8 minutes each; set aside.
Leaving 2 Tbsp fat, cook the onion, poblano and bell pepper 8 to 10 minutes until soft, then the tomatoes about 8 minutes until broken down.
Add the pimentón for 1 minute, then the wine, vinegar, thyme and bay leaves and reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Tuck in the chicken, cover and braise in the oven about 1 hour 15 minutes; discard the thyme and bay leaves.
For the couscous, boil the wine, oil, saffron and 1 cup water and pour over the couscous, currants, onion and salt in a bowl.
Cover and leave about 30 minutes until absorbed, fluff and serve with the chicken.

i: 2 thyme sprigs, plus chopped thyme for garnish
m: Season the drumsticks, dust with 2 Tbsp flour and brown in the oil in a large casserole about 5 minutes; set aside.
Crisp the bacon, then cook the carrot, onion, celery, mushrooms and garlic about 5 minutes until golden.
Add the brandy and reduce by half, stir in the tomato paste and remaining 1 Tbsp flour, then add the wine, stock and thyme sprigs and bring to a boil.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer over low heat about 1½ hours, turning now and then, until very tender; lift out the chicken.
Boil the sauce about 10 minutes until reduced by half and thickened; season and remove the thyme.
Warm the chicken in the sauce, top with chopped thyme and serve. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

i: 2 lbs. chicken wings, cut into 2 pieces at the joints
¼ cup coconut vinegar or unseasoned rice vinegar
m: Toss the wings with 1 Tbsp curry powder and 2 tsp salt, lay them out in a dish with the garlic, pour over the vinegar and fish sauce and marinate overnight in the fridge.
Set up three dishes: cornstarch with 1 tsp salt; eggs whisked with coconut milk; flour mixed with panko, cayenne, both peppers, 1 tsp salt and the remaining curry powder.
Coat each wing in cornstarch, then egg, then the spiced flour.
Fry in two batches in 2 inches of 350° oil about 8 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve with lime wedges.

i: 1 lb. ground chicken, preferably dark meat
⅓ cup minced scallions, plus thinly sliced scallions for garnish
m: Heat the oven to 450° and oil a rimmed baking sheet.
Combine the chicken, breadcrumbs, minced scallions, ginger, egg, garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce and salt.
Shape into 1½-inch balls and set on the sheet.
Brush with oil and bake 13 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Scatter with sliced scallions and serve with chile sauce.

i: 2 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, plus wedges for serving
m: Heat the oven to 450°. Rub the chicken with oil, season and roast in a pan 30 minutes.
Add the sprouts, butter and caraway to the pan and roast 20 minutes more, until the inner thigh reads 165°.
Sprinkle the sprouts with lemon juice and rest the bird 15 minutes.
Carve, toss the sprouts in the pan juices and serve with lemon wedges.

FW|duck confit & white bean stew.t: 45 min active; 1 hr 45 min total, plus overnight soaking
i: 2 cups dried cannellini beans (¾ lb.), soaked overnight and drained
4 purple or orange carrots, sliced ¼ inch thick
2 thyme sprigs, plus leaves for serving
1 small head of radicchio, leaves torn into bite-size pieces
m: Simmer the soaked beans in the broth plus 4 cups water about 1 hour until tender.
Crisp the duck legs in the oil over moderate heat about 15 minutes, then shred the meat and keep the crisp skin aside.
In the same skillet cook the shallots, carrots, garlic, thyme and herbes de Provence about 20 minutes until the shallots caramelize; deglaze with 2 Tbsp water and discard the thyme.
Stir the vegetables into the beans, then add the duck and radicchio.
Serve topped with thyme leaves and the crispy skin. The stew keeps 2 days without the radicchio; add it when reheating.

i: 1 Tbsp. plus 1 tsp. pure olive oil
Four ½-lb. duck breasts, skin and fat removed
6 oz. kumquats, sliced crosswise ⅓ inch thick
m: Marinate the duck 30 minutes in the wine with 1 tsp oil, ½ tsp grainy mustard and ½ tsp rosemary.
Simmer the kumquat slices in water about 5 minutes, drain, then simmer 8 minutes in a syrup of the sugar and ½ cup water; set aside with the syrup.
Season the duck and sear in 1 Tbsp oil over moderately high heat about 3 minutes, then turn and cook 2 to 3 minutes more to medium-rare; keep warm.
Soften the shallots, jalapeño and remaining rosemary in the skillet about 4 minutes.
Add the reserved marinade and reduce to a syrup, then add the kumquats and syrup and bring to a simmer.
Stir in both mustards off the heat, season and spoon over the duck.

i: One 2½-lb. bone-in veal loin roast, bones frenched
4 marjoram sprigs plus 1 Tbsp. chopped marjoram
½ tsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 2 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
m: Heat the oven to 325°. Season the veal and brown it all over in the oil in an ovenproof skillet over high heat, about 4 minutes.
Add the sliced garlic and marjoram sprigs and roast about 45 minutes, turning a couple of times, to 135° in the center.
Rest the meat 15 minutes.
Stir the chopped marjoram and minced garlic into the lemon zest and juice; season.
Carve into ½-inch slices, spoon over the marjoram-lemon mixture and serve with spaetzle or risotto.

i: 1 tsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for frying
4 bacon slices (4 oz.), cut crosswise ¼ inch thick
2 Granny Smith apples, peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
½ small red onion, cut into thin strips
½ lb. dandelion greens, thick stems discarded, leaves cut crosswise into 1-inch pieces
m: Heat the oven to 200°. Beat the eggs with 1 Tbsp water and put the flour and panko in separate bowls.
Season the cutlets, then coat them in flour, egg and panko, pressing the crumbs on.
Fry in ¼ inch of hot olive oil in two batches, about 5 minutes each, turning once; keep warm in the oven.
Wipe the skillet, crisp the bacon in 1 tsp oil, then add the apples and onion and cook about 3 minutes.
Pour in the cider and vinegar and reduce by half, about 3 minutes.
Toss the warm apple mixture with the dandelion greens, season, and pile onto the cutlets.

i: Two 12-oz. flank steaks, about ¾ inch thick
m: Season the steaks well and cook them in 2 Tbsp butter in a very hot cast-iron skillet about 6 minutes total for medium-rare.
Rest the steaks about 10 minutes.
Cook the shallots in 2 Tbsp butter and the oil about 8 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
Add the wine, balsamic and sugar and reduce by half, 3 to 5 minutes.
Whisk in the last 1 Tbsp butter off the heat and season.
Slice the steak across the grain and serve with the sauce.

i: 5 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for tossing and greasing
Two 28-oz. cans whole peeled tomatoes and juices, crushed
m: Heat the oven to 450° and oil a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Parboil the noodles 4 to 5 minutes until just starting to soften, drain and toss with oil on a sheet.
Cook the onion in 2 Tbsp oil about 5 minutes, add the eggplant with the remaining 3 Tbsp oil and cook 3 minutes, then the anchovies and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the olives, capers and tomatoes and boil about 10 minutes until thickened; season.
Mix the ricotta with the eggs and season.
Layer: 1½ cups sauce, 5 noodles, half the ricotta, noodles, half the remaining sauce, noodles, the rest of the ricotta, noodles, the last of the sauce.
Bake covered with foil 40 minutes, uncovered 15 minutes, then top with mozzarella and bake 15 minutes more. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.

i: 6 oz. pancetta, sliced ¼ inch thick and cut crosswise into 1-inch-wide strips
½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
½ cup freshly grated pecorino cheese, plus more for serving
m: Crisp the pancetta in the oil over moderate heat about 7 minutes; drain, keeping 2 Tbsp of the fat.
Simmer the cream in the skillet with plenty of black pepper, stir in the Parmesan and ½ cup pecorino until smooth, then cool.
Whisk the egg yolk, pancetta and reserved fat into the cooled cream and refrigerate.

Bring 4 quarts of water to a boil with the salt. Spread the semolina on a rimmed sheet and flick cold water over it with your fingertips, turning it with a spatula to form pea-size lumps; repeat until nearly all the semolina is lumped.
Shake off loose semolina in a colander, then boil the frascatelli about 4 minutes until al dente.
Gently reheat the sauce, add the drained frascatelli, bring to a simmer and serve with extra pecorino.

i: ¼ lb. sliced bacon, cut crosswise into ¼-inch-wide strips
½ lb. ground beef or a mixture of pork, veal and beef
1 cup beef or chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Render the bacon in the butter over moderately low heat about 3 minutes, then soften the onion about 3 minutes.
Add the beef and cook about 2 minutes until no longer pink.
Pour in the stock and wine, add the tomato paste, oregano, salt and pepper, and simmer about 25 minutes until thick.
Stir in the cream and take off the heat.
Boil the spaghetti about 12 minutes, drain and toss with the sauce and parsley.

i: One 1-inch piece of fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
¼ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
¾ lb. ground beef sirloin (90% lean)
2 plum tomatoes—halved, seeded and finely diced
1 cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese, plus shavings for garnish
m: Blend the garlic, ginger, vinegar, ají amarillo paste, pepper and 1 Tbsp soy sauce into a smooth lomo saltado sauce.
Boil the tagliatelle until al dente and drain.
Brown the beef in the oil over high heat 3 to 4 minutes, breaking it up; lift out.
Soften the onion in the skillet about 5 minutes, return the beef with the tomatoes for 1 minute, add the remaining 2 Tbsp soy sauce and boil 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and the lomo saltado sauce and bring up to a boil.
Toss in the pasta and grated Parmesan, fold in the cilantro, season and serve with Parmesan shavings.

i: ½ lb. calamarata or other short, wide, tubular pasta
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
3 medium red onions, cut into 8 wedges each
6 oz. guanciale or pancetta, cut into ¼-inch dice
¾ cup freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese
¼ small head of radicchio, torn into 2-inch pieces
m: Boil the pasta about 8 minutes until al dente; drain, saving ½ cup of the water.
Toss the onion wedges with salt in ¼ cup hot oil over high heat for 1 minute, add ¾ cup water and cook about 6 minutes until it evaporates and the onions are just tender.
Add the guanciale and cook about 7 minutes until its fat renders and it crisps.
Pour off all but 2 Tbsp fat, add the pasta, pecorino, radicchio and pasta water and stir over high heat about 1 minute.
Season, dot with ricotta, scatter with walnuts, drizzle with oil and serve at once.

i: Four 28-oz. cans whole San Marzano tomatoes—drained, halved lengthwise and seeded
2 cups plus 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
Wide strips of zest from 2 small lemons plus 1 tsp. finely grated zest
Wide strips of zest from 1 small orange
2 marjoram sprigs plus 2 tsp. marjoram leaves
1 lb. paccheri or other wide, tubular pasta
¼ cup freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese, for garnish
m: Toss the tomato halves with the sugar and 4½ tsp salt in a colander and leave to drain 2 hours.
Toast the fennel and coriander seeds about 2 minutes, then grind coarsely.
Warm 2 cups oil with the ground seeds, crushed garlic, zest strips, basil and marjoram sprigs over low heat about 7 minutes until it bubbles; pour over the tomatoes in a deep dish and leave 3 hours.
Lift out the tomatoes and crush coarsely by hand to about 3 cups.
Cook the sliced garlic in the remaining 3 Tbsp oil about 2 minutes, add the tomatoes and red pepper and warm through.
Boil the paccheri until al dente, drain and toss in the sauce with the grated lemon zest and marjoram leaves; top with pecorino.

i: 1½ cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
1 lb. large shrimp, shelled and deveined
1 lb. cleaned small squid—bodies cut crosswise into ½-inch rings, tentacles left whole
m: Soften the onion in the oil about 5 minutes, add the garlic for 2 minutes, then the tomatoes; simmer, add the wine and cook 2 minutes. Season.
Boil the stock, milk and 2 cups water, whisk in the polenta and cook about 2 minutes until slightly thick; stir in 2 Tbsp butter, season and keep warm.
Return the sauce to a simmer and cook the shrimp and squid about 2 minutes.
Add the mussels, cover and cook about 4 minutes until open; discard any closed ones.
Swirl in the last 1 Tbsp butter and the parsley and season.
Ladle the polenta into bowls and spoon the stew over.

FW|pork shank osso buco.t: 1 hr active; 4 hr total, plus overnight salting
i: 2 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Season the shanks with salt and pepper and refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°. Brown the shanks in the oil in two batches, about 8 minutes each, and move to a roasting pan.
Leaving 2 Tbsp fat, cook the onion, carrot and celery with salt and pepper about 10 minutes, then the garlic, anchovies, lemon zest and red pepper until fragrant.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then the tomatoes, stock, thyme, rosemary and bay leaves; bring to a boil and pour over the shanks.
Cover tightly with foil and braise about 3 hours until very tender.
Remove the herbs, skim the fat, puree the sauce smooth and season.
Serve the shanks with the sauce over creamy polenta. Keeps 2 days in the sauce.

i: 2 cups freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese
m: Heat the oven to 350°. Boil the milk with 3 cups water and whisk in the polenta; cook over low heat about 3 minutes until thick.
Whisk in 1½ cups pecorino, the butter and nutmeg; season.
Whisk in the eggs in a thin stream and spread in a 9-by-13-inch dish.
Cover with the tomato sauce and the remaining ½ cup pecorino.
Bake about 20 minutes until bubbling and rest 5 minutes.

i: 8 small skinless, boneless chicken thighs (2 lbs.)
8 garlic cloves, halved lengthwise and lightly smashed
4 large rosemary sprigs, broken into 2-inch pieces
m: Season and flour the thighs, then brown them in the hot oil over high heat about 10 minutes, turning once.
Add the garlic and rosemary for 3 minutes, then move the chicken to a platter.
Pour the stock into the skillet and boil, scraping, about 5 minutes until halved.
Swirl in the lemon juice and butter to emulsify.
Return the chicken with the peppers and turn in the sauce about 3 minutes, then serve.

i: ¾ lb. hot Italian sausages, halved crosswise
3 Italian frying peppers or Cubanelles, halved lengthwise and seeded
2 large red bell peppers, cut into large strips
2 large red onions, cut into 1-inch wedges
2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
m: Heat the oven to 450° and wrap the central tube of a 10-inch Bundt pan in foil.
Toss the sausages, peppers and onions with 2 Tbsp oil and 1 Tbsp oregano, season and put in the pan.
Brush the chicken with oil, season with salt, pepper, the rest of the oregano and the lemon zest, and sit it on the tube.
Roast about 1 hour until the inner thigh reads 155°, then rest 15 minutes.
Pile the sausages, vegetables and juices on a platter, carve the chicken over them and serve with crusty bread.

i: Two 4-lb. racks of pork spareribs, membranes removed
¾ cup packed light brown sugar
m: Heat the oven to 325°. Pound the fennel, thyme, red pepper, rosemary, 1½ Tbsp salt and 2 tsp pepper together and rub over the ribs on foil-lined sheets.
Roast about 2 hours until tender.
Meanwhile soften the onion and garlic in the oil 3 to 5 minutes, add both vinegars, the ketchup and sugar and simmer about 15 minutes down to 2 cups.
Switch to the broiler. Brush the ribs with sauce and broil each sheet 8 inches from the heat until browned on both sides.
Cut into single ribs and pass the remaining sauce. The sauce keeps 1 week.

FW|dry-aged roast beef with fresh hot sa.t: 30 min active; 1 hr 45 min total, plus 1 day curing
i: ½ lb. red Fresno or red jalapeño chiles—stemmed, seeded and coarsely chopped
½ cup very thinly sliced garlic (sliced on a mandoline)
m: Rub the roast with the salt and pepper and leave uncovered in the fridge for a day.
Heat the oven to 400°. Sear the roast in a hot cast-iron skillet, fat side first, about 8 minutes in all until browned everywhere.
Roast fat side up 40 to 45 minutes to 125° for medium-rare and rest 15 minutes.
Blend the hot sauce ingredients smooth and strain.
Bring the garlic slices just to a boil in the milk, drain and dry, then fry in ½ inch of 275° oil 1 to 2 minutes until pale gold; salt them.
Slice the beef thinly over arugula, drizzle with hot sauce and olive oil, top with garlic chips and scallions, and pass the rest of the sauce.

i: 2 large red potatoes, cut into 1½-inch pieces
2 Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch wedges
1 large baking potato, cut into 1½-inch pieces
⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
1½ lbs. sweet Italian sausage, cut into 3-inch lengths
One 8-oz. bunch of arugula, stemmed and chopped
m: Heat the oven to 425°. Toss the potatoes and shallots with ⅓ cup oil on a large sheet and season well.
Roast about 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Brush the sausage with oil, add to the sheet and roast 20 to 25 minutes more until everything is cooked.
Tip onto a platter, fold through the arugula and lemon juice, season and serve.

i: Four 1-inch-thick veal rib chops (about ½ lb. each)
m: Heat the oven to 500°. Toss the grapes with the vinegar, 1½ Tbsp butter and the sugar on a sturdy sheet; season.
Roast about 10 minutes, shaking once, until sizzling.
Rub the chops with the rest of the butter and season.
Push the grapes aside, add the chops and roast 5 minutes, turn and roast 5 minutes more for medium-rare.
Serve the chops with the jammy grapes spooned over.

i: Two 1¼-lb. lamb leg steaks, cut about 1¼ inches thick
1 cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Rub the lamb with cumin and fennel, season, and brown both sides in smoking-hot oil in a cast-iron skillet.
Lower the heat, add the thyme, garlic and 4 Tbsp butter and baste 5 minutes; turn and baste about 5 minutes more to 130°.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice thickly against the grain.
Pour off all but 1 Tbsp fat, soften the shallot 1 minute, add the wine and reduce to a syrup, about 4 minutes.
Add the stock and simmer 3 minutes, then whisk in the last 2 Tbsp butter off the heat and season.
Serve the lamb with the sauce and french fries.
Heat the oven to 375°. Prick the figs and simmer them, covered, in 1 cup water with ⅔ cup port and the lemon zest about 30 minutes until tender; halve the figs and keep the liquid.
Oil the chicken quarters, set skin up in a roasting pan, sprinkle with 1 Tbsp port, season and top each with a piece of butter.
Roast about 30 minutes, take out the breasts, cook the legs 5 minutes more, then return the breasts.
Broil about 2 minutes until the skin is golden.
Pour off the fat, boil the fig liquid in the pan, scraping, about 4 minutes down to ¼ cup, then add the figs, chicken juices and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spoon over the chicken; steamed broccoli is a quick side.

i: ¼ cup sweet Asian chile sauce or hot pepper jelly
¼ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
m: Heat the oven to 425°. Toss the drumsticks with the oil, five-spice, salt and pepper, lay them on a foil-lined sheet and roast about 35 minutes, turning twice.
Blend the hoisin, chile sauce, vinegar, stock, ginger, garlic and sesame oil until smooth, then simmer in a saucepan 5 minutes to thicken slightly.
Coat the roasted drumsticks in the sauce.
Broil 8 inches from the heat for about 10 minutes, turning and brushing with more sauce, until sticky and glazed.
Roll each drumstick in the sesame seeds and serve.
Crosshatch the pork skin, then cut 1-inch-deep slits all over the meat and push a garlic slice into each. Season with 1½ tsp salt and ¾ tsp pepper.
Heat the oil in a 5- to 6-quart slow cooker on high and brown the pork on both sides, 6 to 8 minutes; set aside.
Cook the onion in the cooker, scraping up the browned bits, about 6 minutes until golden.
Return the pork, pour in the cider, cover and cook on low 7 to 8 hours until falling apart.
Shred the meat with two forks, discard the bone, stir the meat back into its juices and season. Pile onto rolls.
Gently mix the four ground meats together by hand and form 4 patties about ¾ inch thick.
Chill the patties on a covered baking sheet at least 2 hours so they firm up.
Heat a grill or grill pan, salt the burgers well and cook over high heat about 3 minutes a side for medium-rare.
Move to a rack, crumble 2 oz of Roquefort over each and rest 3 minutes.
Serve on the toasted buns. Ground skirt steak can stand in for the brisket or short rib.

FW|beef brasato with pappardelle & mint.t: 45 min active; 4 hr total, plus overnight marinating
i: 2¾ lbs. trimmed boneless beef shank, cut into 2-inch pieces
One 35-oz. can peeled Italian tomatoes, crushed
Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, for serving
m: Marinate the beef overnight in the wine with the mint stems, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 325°. Drain the beef (keep the wine, discard the stems), pat dry and brown in two batches in 2 Tbsp oil, about 12 minutes for the first.
Put all the meat back in the pot with the marinade, bring to a boil, add the tomatoes, season and boil again.
Cover and braise in the oven about 2 hours 15 minutes until very tender.
Lift out the meat and shred it; boil the liquid down to 2½ cups, about 20 minutes.
Cook the pappardelle al dente, drain and toss in the pot with the meat and reduced sauce for 2 minutes over moderate heat.
Fry the garlic in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil until lightly golden, add the mint leaves for 10 seconds, pour over the pasta and toss. Serve with Parmigiano.

i: ½ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ lb. rustic bread, cut or torn into 1½-inch pieces
m: Heat the oven to 425°. Trim the top off the garlic head, drizzle with oil, wrap in foil and roast about 45 minutes until soft.
Squeeze out the cloves, mash them smooth and whisk in ¼ cup oil and the vinegar; season with sea salt and pepper.
Toss the bread in ¼ cup oil in a nonstick skillet over moderate heat about 5 minutes until crisp and golden, then divide among plates.
Spiral-cut the filet into a ¼-inch-thick rectangle (or have the butcher butterfly it). Cut shallow slits every 2 inches, rub with 1 Tbsp oil, season and tuck the chives into the slits.
Cook the steak chive side up in a hot cast-iron skillet with 1 Tbsp oil about 3 minutes, flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until the chives char and the meat is medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes.
Top the croutons with basil and microgreens, spoon over the garlic dressing, slice the steak across the grain and serve beside it.

i: Two 1½-lb. bone-in rib eye steaks (1½ inches thick), at room temperature
m: Brush the onion slices with oil, season, and grill over moderate heat about 7 minutes, turning once, until charred and tender.
Boil the vinegar and maple syrup, add the onions and simmer about 8 minutes until soft. Cool, stir in the thyme and season.
Oil and season the steaks. Stand them on their fatty edge over moderate heat about 5 minutes so the fat renders and chars.
Lay the steaks flat and grill, turning often, until the centre reaches 120°, 12 to 15 minutes. Rest 10 minutes.
Mash the butter with rosemary, thyme and garlic, brush it over the steaks and sear over high heat 1 minute a side.
Slice and serve with the onion jam.

i: 1 medium red onion, cut into ⅓-inch dice
1 medium tomato—halved, seeded and cut into ⅓-inch dice
½ red bell pepper, cut into ⅓-inch dice
½ green bell pepper, cut into ⅓-inch dice
½ yellow bell pepper, cut into ⅓-inch dice
1½ lbs. boneless leg of lamb roast
1½ lbs. flanken-cut beef short ribs (cut across the bones), about ½ inch thick
1½ lbs. fresh chorizo or hot Italian sausage
m: Mix the onion, tomato and peppers with the olive oil, lemon juice and a big pinch of salt and pepper; refrigerate overnight.
Stir the parsley into the salsa and let it come to room temperature.
Light a grill. Season the lamb and short ribs and let stand 10 minutes.
Grill everything over moderate heat, turning: the short ribs take about 12 minutes, the chorizo about 15, and the lamb 25 to 35 minutes to reach 130° for medium-rare.
Rest the meats 5 minutes, carve, and serve with the seasoned salsa.

i: 2 Tbsp. canola oil, plus more for brushing
2 Tbsp. finely grated peeled fresh ginger, plus more for garnish
m: Rub the steak and 16 whole scallions with 2 Tbsp oil and season with salt and pepper.
Grill the steak on an oiled grate over moderate heat 20 to 25 minutes, turning, until it reaches 125° for medium-rare. Rest 15 minutes.
Grill the whole scallions about 3 minutes until charred and tender; set 8 aside on a platter and chop the rest.
Mix the chopped scallions with the 2 sliced raw ones, the cilantro, chiles, lime juice and ginger.
Slice the steak thinly across the grain, spoon the relish on top and finish with freshly grated ginger.
Combine the seven spices; keep back 2 tsp for the sauce and rub the rest over the chops. Leave 15 minutes at room temperature.
Salt the chops and cook in 2 Tbsp oil in a cast-iron skillet over moderate heat 3 to 4 minutes a side, to 125° inside. Rest 5 minutes on plates.
Pour off all but 1 Tbsp of fat, cook the garlic over low heat 1 minute, then stir in the reserved spices for 1 minute.
Add the sherry and whisk in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil; season.
Spoon the sauce over the lamb and scatter with parsley.

FW|leg of lamb shawarma.t: 30 min active; 3 hr total, plus overnight marinating
i: 1 head of garlic, top fourth cut off
2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
Finely grated zest and juice of 2 lemons
Grilled flatbread, plain yogurt mixed with dill and sliced cucumbers, for serving
m: Drizzle the garlic head with oil, wrap in foil and bake at 350° about 1 hour 15 minutes until very soft.
Mash the squeezed-out cloves with the lemon zest and juice, paprika, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, 2 Tbsp oil, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper.
Cut ½-inch-deep slits all over the lamb, rub the paste in thoroughly and refrigerate overnight.
Bring the lamb to room temperature, season, and grill fat side down over moderately high heat about 20 minutes until charred.
Turn and grill about 20 minutes more, to 130° in the thickest part. Rest 15 minutes.
Carve thinly and serve in grilled flatbread with dilled yogurt and cucumber.

i: ¼ cup packed light brown sugar
3¾ lbs. flanken-style beef short ribs, sliced ⅓ inch thick
Lemon wedges and coleslaw, for serving
m: Stir together the brown sugar, salt, paprika, chili powder, garlic salt, oregano and pepper.
Coat the short ribs in the rub and leave 20 minutes.
Heat the grill and oil the grate.
Grill the ribs over high heat about 6 minutes, turning once, until well charred and just cooked.
Serve with lemon wedges and coleslaw.

i: ½ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
¼ cup small mint leaves and a large pinch of pimentón de la Vera, for garnish
m: Pulse the rosemary and garlic with a pinch of salt and pepper in a blender, then stream in ½ cup oil until finely chopped.
Coat the chops in the paste in a baking dish and refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight.
Season the chops and grill over high heat about 6 minutes, turning once, until charred and medium-rare.
Rest 5 minutes on a platter.
Scatter with mint and pimentón, drizzle with oil and serve at once.

i: Two 2½- to 3-lb. racks of lamb ribs
m: Mix the salt, sugar, cumin, coriander, pepper and cinnamon; set aside 2 Tbsp.
Massage the rest of the rub into the lamb ribs and leave at room temperature 1 hour.
Whisk the vinegar and pomegranate molasses into the reserved rub to make a basting sauce.
Grill the ribs meaty side down over moderately low heat 7 to 10 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred.
Lower the heat and grill about 1 hour 30 minutes, turning and basting every 10 minutes, until very tender.
Tent with foil 10 minutes, then cut between the bones.

i: One 1½-lb. pork tenderloin, cut in half crosswise and tied (have your butcher do this)
m: Rub the pork with nutmeg, season well, slip the garlic and sage under the strings and leave 30 minutes.
Brown the pork all over in 2 Tbsp butter and the oil over high heat, about 7 minutes; set aside.
Leave 2 Tbsp fat in the skillet and brown the onion, carrot, thyme and bay leaf with salt and pepper, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the wine for 1 minute, then the stock; bring to a boil, return the pork, cover and braise gently 13 to 15 minutes to 135°. Rest 10 minutes.
Strain the liquid, bring back to a simmer, take off the heat and whisk in the honey and last 1 Tbsp butter; season.
Untie, slice and serve with the sauce.

i: Generous pinch of crushed red pepper
One ¼-lb. piece of mortadella, cut into small dice
1 lb. fresh mozzarella, cut into bite-size pieces
m: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil, add the pork and brown it about 10 minutes, breaking it up.
Cook off the wine, add the tomatoes, red pepper and salt, and simmer about 1 hour until thick.
Hard-boil the eggs 8 minutes, cool, peel and chop finely.
Heat the oven to 425°. Cook the macaroni al dente and stir into the ragù with the herbs, eggs, mortadella, three-quarters of the mozzarella and ¾ cup Parmigiano.
Tip into a 3-quart baking dish, top with the remaining cheeses and bake about 25 minutes until hot. Stand 5 minutes.
The assembled, unbaked dish can be refrigerated overnight; bring to room temperature before baking.

i: ½ cup frozen artichoke hearts, thawed and sliced ½ inch thick
½ lb. pizza dough, thawed if frozen
¼ lb. fresh mozzarella, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 oz. thinly sliced baked ham, cut into 1-inch strips
½ cup fresh ricotta cheese (4 oz.)
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. marinara sauce
2 large cremini mushrooms, sliced ¼ inch thick
4 pitted olives, sliced ¼ inch thick
m: Heat a pizza stone in a 500° oven for 30 minutes. Season the artichokes with oil, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough into a 12-inch round, ⅛ inch thick, thinning the edge on one half, and set on a floured peel; brush with oil.
On the thinner half, 3 inches in from the edge, layer half the mozzarella and ham, all the ricotta and salami, half the oregano and 2 Tbsp marinara.
Fold the edge over the filling and press it down in the centre to seal, making a half calzone.
Spread the remaining ¼ cup marinara over the open dough, add the rest of the mozzarella and ham, the artichokes, mushrooms, olives and oregano.
Bake on the stone 8 to 10 minutes until crisp and bubbling, then cut into wedges.

i: 6 baking apples, such as Gala, quartered and cored
m: Heat the oven to 400°. Score the pork skin in a crosshatch and set it skin side up in a roasting pan.
Grind the bay leaves, juniper, ¼ cup salt and 2 tsp pepper to a powder and rub it all over the pork and into the skin.
Roast 30 minutes, drop the oven to 325° and roast about 6½ hours more until the meat is very tender and the skin crisp. Rest 30 minutes.
Toss the apples with the oil, cinnamon sticks, salt and pepper and roast about 30 minutes, tossing once; discard the cinnamon.
Chop the crisp skin, pull the meat into large pieces, discarding fat and bones, and serve topped with the skin alongside the apples.

FW|pan-roasted veal chops with cabernet.t: 20 min active; 1 hr 20 min total, plus overnight marinating
i: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
m: Marinate the chops overnight in ¼ cup oil with the thyme and garlic.
Boil the wine with half the shallots down to ½ cup, about 15 minutes.
Cook the remaining shallot in the butter until golden, stir in the flour, whisk in the stock and boil until thick.
Whisk the reduced wine into the sauce and simmer 30 minutes, then strain and season.
Heat the oven to 325°. Wipe the garlic off the chops, season, and sear in 2 Tbsp oil over high heat about 3 minutes a side.
Roast in the skillet about 10 minutes, turning once, until just pink in the centre; serve with the sauce. The sauce keeps 3 days in the fridge.

i: 2 lbs. skirt steak, cut into 5-inch lengths
4 medium leeks (2½ lbs.), white and light green parts only, halved lengthwise and cleaned
m: Warm the coriander, both peppercorns and red pepper in the butter over moderately low heat 1 minute; stir in the sugar and 1½ Tbsp salt.
Rub the spiced butter over the steak, cover and chill 3 hours.
Blanch the leeks in salted water 3 to 4 minutes until just tender and drain cut side down on paper towels.
Whisk the mustard with the vinegar.
Sear the steak in two batches in a smoking-hot cast-iron skillet with 1 Tbsp oil each, 4 to 5 minutes, until charred outside and medium-rare. Spread with the Dijon mix and rest 10 minutes.
Char the leeks cut side down in the last 1 Tbsp oil about 3 minutes, sprinkle with lemon juice and serve with the sliced steak.

i: 1 medium baking potato (8 oz.), peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces
⅓ cup plus 1 Tbsp. whole milk
⅓ cup plus 1 Tbsp. heavy cream
¾ cup plus 2 Tbsp. plain dry breadcrumbs
Mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam, for serving
m: Boil the potato in salted water about 12 minutes, drain, rice it and let cool.
Heat the oven to 425°. Whisk the egg with the milk and cream, stir in the breadcrumbs and let them soak 5 minutes.
Add the beef, pork, onion, salt, white pepper and riced potato, mix lightly and roll into 18 balls.
Brown the meatballs in two batches, 2 Tbsp butter each, over moderate heat about 8 minutes per batch, wiping the ovenproof skillet between batches.
Return all the meatballs to the skillet and bake about 10 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam. The raw meatballs can be refrigerated overnight.

i: Two 4-oz. pieces of dry Spanish chorizo
6 cups dry red wine (about two 750-ml bottles)
m: Put the chorizo, wine, garlic, bay leaves and cayenne in a large skillet and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over moderately low heat about 15 minutes, turning the chorizo once, until plump; stand uncovered 5 minutes.
Slice the chorizo ¼ inch thick on the diagonal and simmer the slices in the wine 5 minutes more over low heat.
Pile the slices in a shallow bowl, add poaching liquid to come halfway up, and serve with toothpicks.

i: Two 12- to 14-oz. New York strip steaks, about 1¼ inches thick, at room temperature for 30 minutes
1 white onion, cut into 8 wedges through the core
m: Brush the steaks and onion wedges with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Rub one onion wedge over the hot grate, then grill the steaks and remaining onion, covered, over moderately high heat 6 to 7 minutes, turning once, until medium-rare and the onion is tender.
Rest the steaks and onion at least 10 minutes.
Put the steaks back on the grill about 2 minutes, turning once, just to reheat the surface.
Slice across the grain and serve with the grilled onion.

i: 8 piquillo peppers (Spanish roasted peppers), seeded and chopped
m: Mix the paprika, brown sugar, 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper and pat it over the steak.
Soften the garlic, shallots and capers in the olive oil over moderate heat about 3 minutes, then add the sage for 1 minute.
Stir in the piquillos, mustard and Worcestershire and simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Grill the steak over moderately high heat about 12 minutes, turning once, to 130° for medium-rare.
Rest 5 minutes, slice and serve with the piquillo sauce.

i: 4 oz. Maytag blue cheese, crumbled into ½-inch chunks (1 cup)
m: Heat the oven to 350°. Spread the tomatoes on one sheet with ½ cup wine, 2 Tbsp olive oil and 2 thyme sprigs; spread the shallots on another with 1½ Tbsp oil and 2 thyme sprigs. Season both and bake about 40 minutes until very soft.
Raise the oven to 425°. Season the tenderloin and brown it in the vegetable oil in an ovenproof skillet, about 4 minutes, then turn and cook 3 minutes more.
Roast 10 minutes, turn, and roast another 10 minutes to 125° for medium-rare. Rest 10 minutes.
Pour off the fat, deglaze the skillet with the remaining ½ cup wine and reduce by half, about 3 minutes; stir in the tomatoes, shallots and their juices off the heat.
Slice the beef ⅓ inch thick, spoon over the vegetables and sauce, and dot with the blue cheese.

i: 2 lbs. trimmed boneless beef short ribs, cut into 8 equal pieces
3 slices of bacon, cut into 1-inch pieces
4 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
½ lb. carrots, peeled and cut into ½-inch pieces
½ lb. rutabaga, peeled and cut into ½-inch pieces
½ lb. butternut squash, peeled and cut into ½-inch pieces
½ lb. parsnips, peeled and cut into ½-inch pieces
½ lb. celery root, peeled and cut into ½-inch pieces
1 Tbsp. chopped parsley, plus more for garnish
m: Season and flour the short ribs and brown them in the oil in a large casserole, about 8 minutes; set aside.
Cook the butter, bacon, garlic head, onions, shallots, thyme and bay leaves 5 minutes until golden, then add the wine and port and reduce by half, about 5 minutes.
Return the ribs with their juices, add the stock, cover and simmer on low about 2 hours until very tender.
Strain the sauce, pressing on the solids, reduce it by a third (about 15 minutes) and warm the ribs in it 5 minutes.
For the mash, sweat the root vegetables with the garlic, thyme and bay in 4 Tbsp butter 10 minutes, add the honey, cover and cook 15 minutes.
Add 1 cup water and cook covered about 20 minutes until nearly dry; remove the herbs, stir in the last 1 Tbsp butter, mash coarsely with a fork, fold in the parsley and season.
Plate the mash, set the ribs on top, garnish with parsley and pass the sauce.

i: 2 Tbsp. pickled ginger, sliced into thin strips
m: Marinate the sliced steak 15 minutes in the sherry, soy sauce and cornstarch.
Whisk together the broth, sherry, oyster, hoisin and chile-garlic sauces and cornstarch for the sauce.
Drain the beef and stir-fry it in 2 Tbsp oil in a very hot wok about 1 minute until browned and medium; remove.
Stir-fry the fresh ginger and scallions in the last 1 Tbsp oil about 30 seconds.
Return the beef with the pickled ginger and sauce and toss about 10 seconds until the sauce thickens.
Serve in bowls with steamed rice or lo mein noodles.

i: 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
Flaky sea salt, such as Maldon, for serving
m: Heat the oven to 350°. Stir the salt and tarragon into the water until slushy and just holding together when squeezed.
Shape half the salt into two ovals a little bigger than the racks at each end of a roasting pan.
Brown the racks in 3 Tbsp oil over moderately high heat, 4 minutes on the meaty side and 2 minutes on each other side, then set them on the salt beds and cool briefly.
Pack the rest of the salt over and around the lamb to cover it completely and roast 25 minutes, to 135° inside. Rest 5 minutes.
Crack off the crust, brush away the salt, brush with oil and cut into chops; finish with flaky salt. Serve with sautéed Swiss chard.

i: 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for the roux
3½ lbs. boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
4 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
½ lb. medium carrots, cut into 2-inch pieces
Chopped parsley and mint, for garnish
m: Season the lamb and brown it in 3 Tbsp oil in three batches, about 8 minutes each; set aside.
Brown the onions about 5 minutes, then the garlic about 2 minutes, and add them to the lamb.
Off the heat, top up the fat to 6 Tbsp with oil and whisk in the flour; add the wine and simmer, scraping the pot.
Whisk in 4 cups water and the stock, return the lamb and onions, cover and simmer gently about 1 hour 45 minutes until tender.
Add the turnips, carrots and potatoes and cook about 30 minutes more until tender; stir in the cream and season.
Ladle into bowls, top with parsley and mint and serve with crusty bread. Keeps 3 days refrigerated.
